title.raw: 卷138 志一百十三 兵九 海防

sentences.zh: 志一百十三

translations.literal: Treatise 113.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 113

sentences.zh: 兵九

translations.literal: Military 9.
translations.idiomatic: Military 9

sentences.zh: 海防

translations.literal: Coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal Defense

sentences.zh: 國初海防，僅備海盜而已。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty, coastal defense was only prepared against sea pirates.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qing, coastal defense amounted to little more than guarding against pirates.

sentences.zh: 自道光中海禁大開，形勢一變，海防益重。

translations.literal: From the Daoguang era the maritime prohibition was greatly relaxed, the situation changed entirely, and coastal defense became increasingly important.
translations.idiomatic: Once the maritime ban was largely lifted under the Daoguang Emperor, the strategic picture shifted, and coastal defense grew far more pressing.

sentences.zh: 海防向分南北洋。

translations.literal: Coastal defense was formerly divided into the Northern and Southern Seas.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal defense had long been organized under the Northern and Southern Seas commands.

sentences.zh: 山東煙台歸北洋兼轄。

translations.literal: Yantai in Shandong fell under the concurrent jurisdiction of the Northern Seas.
translations.idiomatic: Yantai in Shandong was placed under the Northern Seas command.

sentences.zh: 閩、浙、粵三口，歸南洋兼轄。

translations.literal: The three ports of Fujian, Zhejiang, and Guangdong fell under the concurrent jurisdiction of the Southern Seas.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian, Zhejiang, and Guangdong ports came under the Southern Seas command.

sentences.zh: 茲取沿海各省有海防者分述之：曰東三省，曰直隸，曰山東，曰江南，附江防，曰浙江，曰福建，曰廣東。

translations.literal: Here the coastal provinces that had coastal defense are taken up and described separately: namely the Three Eastern Provinces, Zhili, Shandong, Jiangnan with river defense appended, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: What follows is a province-by-province account of coastal defense along the seaboard: the Three Eastern Provinces, Zhili, Shandong, Jiangnan (with a section on river defense), Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 奉天沿海，南自牛庄至金、蓋各州，轉東至鴨綠江口，西則自山海關至錦州，地皆濱海，口岸凡三十九處。

translations.literal: Along the Fengtian coast, from Niuzhuang in the south to the Jin and Gai prefectures, turning east to the mouth of the Yalu River, and in the west from Shanhaiguan to Jinzhou—all lands bordering the sea—with thirty-nine ports in all.
translations.idiomatic: Fengtian's coastline ran south from Niuzhuang through the Jin and Gai prefectures, east to the Yalu estuary, and west from Shanhaiguan to Jinzhou; the entire region fronted the sea, with thirty-nine ports along it.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，廷議錦州一帶籌備沿邊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangxi reign, the court debated preparations along the border in the Jinzhou region.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign, the court took up plans to fortify the Jinzhou frontier.

sentences.zh: 旋定金州旅順口設水師戰船，隸金州副都統督率訓練，戰船皆木質舊式。

translations.literal: Soon afterward warships of the naval forces were established at Jinzhou's Lüshunkou; they were subordinate to the Jinzhou deputy lieutenant-general, who supervised training; the warships were all old-style wooden vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Naval warships were then stationed at Lüshunkou near Jinzhou, placed under the Jinzhou deputy lieutenant-general for training—all of them old-fashioned wooden craft.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，將軍噶爾弼以自旅順海口至鳳凰城，水程千里，僅恃旅順水師一營，議增二營，聯絡巡哨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, General Ga'erbi noted that from Lüshun harbor to Fengcheng the water route was a thousand li, yet only one battalion of the Lüshun naval force was relied upon; he proposed adding two battalions to link patrols.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 (1726), General Ga'erbi argued that the thousand-li water route from Lüshun to Fengcheng could not be covered by a single Lüshun naval battalion and urged two more battalions to coordinate patrols along the coast.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年，耆英以奉省海防經營不易，有移民內徙之議，海防漸重。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang, Qiying, because Fengtian's coastal defense was hard to manage, proposed relocating immigrants inland; coastal defense gradually grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 (1841), Qiying, finding Fengtian's coastal defenses difficult to sustain, floated a plan to move settlers inland, and coastal defense there steadily gained weight.

sentences.zh: 咸豐之季，歐艦北犯津、沽，奉天亦嚴海防。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xianfeng reign, European warships invaded north toward Tianjin and Dagu; Fengtian also tightened coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xianfeng era, as European fleets pushed north against Tianjin and Dagu, Fengtian likewise tightened its coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，崇厚調天津洋槍隊千人赴營口屯駐。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi, Chonghou transferred a thousand men of the Tianjin foreign-rifle corps to garrison at Yingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 4 (1865), Chonghou sent a thousand men of the Tianjin foreign-rifle corps to garrison Yingkou.

sentences.zh: 五年，以奉天兵船拙重，調天津輕利兵船十餘艘赴長島駐防。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because Fengtian's gunboats were clumsy and heavy, more than ten light and agile gunboats from Tianjin were transferred to garrison at Changdao.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, because Fengtian's gunboats were too slow and unwieldy, more than ten nimble gunboats from Tianjin were posted to Changdao.

sentences.zh: 復增新練洋槍隊五百人於營口。

translations.literal: Five hundred men of a newly trained foreign-rifle corps were again added at Yingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Another five hundred men of a newly trained foreign-rifle corps were added at Yingkou.

sentences.zh: 十一年，瑞麟以南洋自制兵艦告成，砲械咸備，乃商撥兵艦一艘，巡防牛庄海口。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Ruilin reported that the Southern Seas' domestically built warship was completed and ordnance fully supplied; he then negotiated the allocation of one warship to patrol the Niuzhuang harbor mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 11 (1872), Ruilin reported that a Southern Seas warship built in China was ready and fully armed, and secured one vessel to patrol the mouth of Niuzhuang harbor.

sentences.zh: 光緒初年，以俄羅斯有窺北邊，沿海亦有俄艦游弋，乃於制兵外加餉練兵，凡選練馬步隊四千二百餘人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign, because Russia was casting eyes on the northern frontier and Russian warships also cruised along the coast, paid drill troops were added beyond the regular establishment; in all more than 4,200 cavalry and infantry were selected and trained.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu era, with Russia eyeing the northern frontier and Russian warships patrolling the coast, the province raised paid drill troops on top of the regular rolls, mustering more than 4,200 cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 又增綠營兵四千人，調撥吉林、黑龍江、蒙古馬隊各二百餘人駐營口，與宋慶豫軍協同防守。

translations.literal: Four thousand Green Standard troops were also added; more than two hundred cavalry each from Jilin, Heilongjiang, and Mongolia were transferred to garrison at Yingkou, cooperating in defense with Song Qing's Henan army.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand Green Standard troops were added, and cavalry detachments of more than two hundred men each from Jilin, Heilongjiang, and Mongolia were posted to Yingkou to cooperate with Song Qing's Henan army.

sentences.zh: 其東邊道之練軍馬步隊一千三百人，則分駐鳳凰城、大孤山、北河、長甸河口及安東等處。

translations.literal: The Eastern Frontier Circuit's drilled army of 1,300 cavalry and infantry were then distributed to garrison at Fengcheng, Dagushan, Beihe, the Changdian River mouth, Andong, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Some 1,300 drilled cavalry and infantry of the Eastern Frontier Circuit were stationed at Fengcheng, Dagushan, Beihe, the Changdian estuary, Andong, and other posts.

sentences.zh: 額設正兵，幾同虛設，海上有警，全恃客軍。

translations.literal: The quota regular troops were nearly a dead letter; when there was alarm at sea, everything depended on guest armies.
translations.idiomatic: The regular quota troops were largely nominal; at sea any real alarm had to be met by outside forces.

sentences.zh: 金州與海參威毗連之處，尤為重要。

translations.literal: The place where Jinzhou adjoined Vladivostok was especially important.
translations.idiomatic: The stretch where Jinzhou bordered Vladivostok was especially critical.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章遣鎮東等四砲艦巡防奉省海口。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang dispatched four gunboats including the Zhendong to patrol the harbors of Fengtian province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang sent four gunboats, including the Zhendong, to patrol Fengtian's harbors.

sentences.zh: 八年，鴻章以北洋迤東口岸，惟奉天旅順口為首沖，乃在旅順之黃金山頂，仿築德國新式砲台，設巨砲多尊，並建築兵房、子藥庫，近山要路，復設行營砲壘，海口內則布置水雷，沿海岸可登陸處，擇要埋藏地雷，陸路則有護軍營八哨，毅軍十一營，水路則有快砲船、蚊砲船各二艘，表裡依護。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Hongzhang, because among the Northern Seas' eastern ports only Fengtian's Lüshunkou was the foremost point of impact, built on the Huangjin Hilltop at Lüshun new-style forts modeled on Germany's, setting up many heavy guns, and also constructing barracks and powder magazines; on important roads near the hills he further set field gun redoubts; inside the harbor mouth he laid naval mines; along the coast at places where landing was possible he selected key points to bury land mines; on land there were eight outposts of the Guard Army and eleven battalions of the Yi Army; on water there were two fast gunboats and two mosquito gunboats each, protecting inner and outer approaches.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8 (1882), Li Hongzhang judged Lüshunkou the critical hinge among the Northern Seas' eastern ports and on Huangjin Hill built German-style forts mounting heavy guns, with barracks and magazines, field batteries on nearby passes, mines in the harbor, and buried land mines at likely landing beaches; eight Guard Army outposts and eleven Yi Army battalions covered the landward side, while two fast gunboats and two mosquito craft guarded the water—defense in depth by land and sea.

sentences.zh: 其次為營口，海灘平衍，敵易抄襲，復調勁旅接應後路。

translations.literal: Next was Yingkou, where the beach was flat and extended and the enemy could easily outflank; elite troops were again transferred to support the rear route.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkou came next: its beaches were broad and flat, inviting flanking landings, so strong reinforcements were posted to cover the rear.

sentences.zh: 十年，將軍定安於營口創設水雷營，電線火藥，建雷庫十間存儲。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, General Ding'an established a naval mine battalion at Yingkou, with electric-wire explosives, building ten mine storehouses for storage.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 (1884), General Ding'an set up a mine battalion at Yingkou with electric detonation gear and ten magazines to hold the charges.

sentences.zh: 十七年，李鴻章以大連灣為渤海門戶，築老龍頭等處砲台六座，仿西洋曲折式，兵房、藥庫皆備。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Li Hongzhang, taking Dalian Bay as the gateway to the Bohai, built six forts at places including Laolongtou, modeled on the Western zigzag style, with barracks and magazines all provided.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 17 (1891), Li Hongzhang treated Dalian Bay as the Bohai's outer gate and built six zigzag-style Western forts at Laolongtou and elsewhere, complete with barracks and magazines.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，將軍增祺以岫岩、安東沿海，雖有北洋兵艦巡防，而海濱港汊紛歧，乃增造大號水師船八艘，布列於沙河、大孤山、太平溝等處。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, General Zengqi, because along the Xiuyan and Andong coast, although Northern Seas warships patrolled, the seaside harbors and inlets were numerous and branching, added eight large naval vessels and deployed them at Shahe, Dagushan, Taipinggou, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 26 (1900), General Zengqi found the Xiuyan and Andong coast, though patrolled by Beiyang warships, riddled with creeks and inlets, and added eight large patrol craft posted at Shahe, Dagushan, Taipinggou, and similar anchorages.

sentences.zh: 至吉林、黑龍江之海防，以有松花、黑龍二江，貫省境而趨海，舊制二省各設水師營巡防，水師船止運船三十艘，槳船二十艘，每為運糧及采東珠、取樺皮之用，亦稱水手營，非戰艦也。

translations.literal: As for coastal defense in Jilin and Heilongjiang, because the Songhua and Amur rivers ran through the provinces to the sea, under the old system each province set up a naval battalion for patrol; the naval vessels were only thirty transport ships and twenty oared boats, mostly for transporting grain, collecting eastern pearls, and gathering birch bark—also called sailor battalions, not warships.
translations.idiomatic: Jilin and Heilongjiang coastal defense centered on the Songhua and Amur, which cut through both provinces to the sea. Each province once maintained a naval patrol battalion, but its thirty transports and twenty oared craft served grain haulage, pearl fishing, and birch-bark collection—the so-called sailor corps, not fighting ships.

sentences.zh: 吉林海防，首重琿春。

translations.literal: Jilin's coastal defense placed Hunchun foremost.
translations.idiomatic: For Jilin, coastal defense hinged above all on Hunchun.

sentences.zh: 松花江雖可行海舶，而江水淺處為多。

translations.literal: Although seagoing vessels could navigate the Songhua River, shallow stretches were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Seagoing ships could enter the Songhua, but much of the river was too shallow.

sentences.zh: 同治四年以後，屢有俄羅斯兵船，乘江水漲時，駛入至阿勒楚喀及伯都訥境內。

translations.literal: After the fourth year of Tongzhi, Russian gunboats repeatedly, when the river rose, sailed in as far as the territory of Aletuheka and Boduna.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongzhi 4 (1865), Russian gunboats repeatedly steamed upriver at high water as far as Aletuheka and Boduna.

sentences.zh: 將軍岐元擬於三姓設水師營，不果。

translations.literal: General Qiyuan proposed establishing a naval battalion at Sanxing; it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: General Qiyuan proposed a naval battalion at Sanxing, but the plan failed.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，府丞王家璧有整頓東省水師改造戰艦之議。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu, Vice Prefect Wang Jiabi proposed reorganizing the eastern provinces' naval forces and converting vessels into warships.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 (1880), Vice Prefect Wang Jiabi urged reorganizing the eastern provinces' river flotilla into proper warships.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章以長江水師船不適用於松花、黑龍二江，宜于吉林、三姓左近，擇水深溜大之處設船廠，造小號兵輪船，如廣東蚊砲船之式，入水不深，上可行駛伯都訥、省城附近，下可巡行黑河口，轉入黑龍江，以佐陸軍，備俄船侵入。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang held that Yangtze naval vessels were unsuited to the Songhua and Amur; a shipyard should be set up near Jilin and Sanxing where the water was deep and the current strong, building small gunboats of the Guangdong mosquito-gunboat type, with shallow draft—upstream they could reach Boduna and the area near the provincial capital, downstream patrol the Amur mouth and enter the Heilongjiang, to assist the land army against Russian incursion by ship.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang argued that Yangtze gunboats would not do on the Songhua and Amur; instead a yard near Jilin and Sanxing should build shallow-draft mosquito gunboats like those of Guangdong—able to reach Boduna and the capital upstream, patrol the Amur mouth downstream, and enter the Heilongjiang to back the land forces against Russian river incursions.

sentences.zh: 並撥開花砲、新式馬槍、快槍等，為吉省練兵之用。

translations.literal: Shell guns, new-style muskets, and rapid-fire rifles were also allocated for Jilin's troop drilling.
translations.idiomatic: Shell guns, breech-loading muskets, and rapid-fire rifles were also issued for drilling Jilin's troops.

sentences.zh: 時將軍銘安、及督辦寧古塔等處防務吳大澂、喜昌，以俄患未平，于吉省沿江沿邊，增練防軍馬步隊五千人，各旗及西丹又募千五百人，練成即赴琿春駐守，並設護江關，防範水路。

translations.literal: At that time General Ming'an and Wu Dacheng and Xichang, who supervised defense at Ningguta and other places, because the Russian threat was not settled, along Jilin's rivers and borders added drill of 5,000 cavalry and infantry of defense troops; banners and Xidan also recruited 1,500; once trained they went to garrison at Hunchun and established river-guard passes to guard the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: General Ming'an, together with Wu Dacheng and Xichang, who oversaw defenses at Ningguta and elsewhere, raised 5,000 drilled frontier cavalry and infantry along Jilin's rivers and borders, with another 1,500 recruited from the banners and Xidan; once trained they garrisoned Hunchun and river-guard posts were set up to control the waterways.

sentences.zh: 又慮俄國海軍船堅力猛，水關不能阻其衝突，乃擇要依山建築砲台，以御俄艦。

translations.literal: They also feared that Russian naval vessels were stout and powerful and that water passes could not block their breakthrough; therefore they selected key points along hills to build forts against Russian ships.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Russia's tough seagoing hulls might smash through river barriers, they also built hilltop batteries at key points to engage Russian warships.

sentences.zh: 黑龍江省於光緒三年始籌辦海防，通省額兵及西丹共一萬人，增鄂倫春兵五百人，兼習新式槍砲。

translations.literal: Heilongjiang province began planning coastal defense in the third year of Guangxu; quota troops and Xidan throughout the province totaled ten thousand; five hundred Oroqen troops were added, also practicing new-style guns and cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Heilongjiang began coastal-defense planning in Guangxu 3 (1877), with ten thousand regular and Xidan troops province-wide plus five hundred Oroqen trained in modern firearms.

sentences.zh: 黑省近俄，俄人環黑龍江左岸盤踞，達二千餘里，每相間百餘里，輒有俄兵屯駐之所，刁斗相聞。

translations.literal: Heilongjiang bordered Russia; Russians entrenched along the left bank of the Amur for more than two thousand li; every hundred-odd li apart there were places where Russian troops were stationed, watch-drums audible to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Heilongjiang pressed against Russia: along more than two thousand li of the Amur's left bank Russian posts stood roughly every hundred li, their watch-drums within earshot of one another.

sentences.zh: 故黑省防務，重在陸而不在海。

translations.literal: Therefore Heilongjiang's defense lay chiefly on land, not on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Heilongjiang's defense therefore weighed on land, not sea power.

sentences.zh: 其江流入海之口，在省境東北隅，雖額設師船三十餘艘，僅循例操演。

translations.literal: Where its river entered the sea lay the province's northeastern corner; although more than thirty naval vessels were on the rolls, they only went through routine drill.
translations.idiomatic: The river mouth lay in the province's northeast; though more than thirty vessels were on the books, they saw only routine exercises.

sentences.zh: 東三省海防，奉天尤重。

translations.literal: Among the Three Eastern Provinces' coastal defense, Fengtian was especially weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Three Eastern Provinces, Fengtian bore the heaviest coastal-defense burden.

sentences.zh: 自日佔旅、大，遼東半島籓籬盡撤。

translations.literal: Since Japan occupied Lüshun and Dalian, the Liaodong Peninsula's protective screen was wholly removed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Japan seized Lüshun and Dalian, the Liaodong Peninsula lost its outer shield entirely.

sentences.zh: 而吉、黑二省，向受俄患，北海屢警，防務益形棘手雲。

translations.literal: Yet Jilin and Heilongjiang had long suffered Russian trouble; the northern sea was repeatedly alarmed, and defense grew ever more difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jilin and Heilongjiang, long menaced by Russia, faced repeated alarms on the northern seas, and their defenses grew ever harder to sustain.

sentences.zh: 直隸津、沽口，為南北運河、永定、大清、子牙五河入海處，北連遼東，有旅順、大連以為左翼，南走登、萊，有威海衛以為右翼，為北洋第一重鎮。

translations.literal: Zhili's Tianjin and Dagu mouths were where the north-south canal and the Yongding, Daqing, and Ziya rivers entered the sea; to the north connecting with Liaodong, with Lüshun and Dalian as the left wing; southward toward Deng and Lai, with Weihaiwei as the right wing—the foremost strongpoint of the Northern Seas.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili's Tianjin and Dagu mouths, where the Grand Canal and the Yongding, Daqing, and Ziya rivers reach the sea, anchored the Northern Seas command: Lüshun and Dalian guarded the north, Weihaiwei the south along the Dengzhou–Laizhou coast—the system's primary fortress.

sentences.zh: 順治初，天津巡撫雷興疏言，大沽海口為神京門戶，請置戰船以備海防。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, Tianjin governor Lei Xing memorialized that the Dagu harbor mouth was the divine capital's gateway and requested warships for coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, Tianjin governor Lei Xing urged that Dagu guarded the capital's maritime gate and asked for warships to strengthen coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 下所司議行。

translations.literal: It was referred down to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices for action.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，于海口蘆家嘴創設天津水師營，令滿洲兵丁駐紮，學習水師，特簡都統大員，守御海口。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, at Lujiazui on the harbor mouth the Tianjin naval battalion was established; Manchu soldiers were stationed to learn naval service; a specially selected lieutenant-general was appointed to guard the harbor mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 (1726) a Tianjin naval battalion was founded at Lujiazui, with Manchu troops trained for river and sea duty under a specially appointed lieutenant-general to hold the harbor.

sentences.zh: 復自天津城南門外起至慶雲縣止，所有沿海各州縣，設立海撥二十五處，分置守兵，扼要防範。

translations.literal: Further, from outside Tianjin's south gate to Qingyun county, along all coastal prefectures and counties, twenty-five coastal patrol posts were set up, garrison troops distributed, guarding key points.
translations.idiomatic: From Tianjin's south gate to Qingyun, twenty-five coastal patrol posts were established along the seaboard counties, each with troops at critical points.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年，直隸總督高斌請拓天津水師營、汛，增駐滿兵一千，合舊額為三千。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong, Zhili governor Gao Bin requested expanding the Tianjin naval battalion and garrison posts, adding a thousand Manchu troops, totaling three thousand with the old quota.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 4 (1739), Zhili governor Gao Bin asked to enlarge the Tianjin naval battalion and posts by a thousand Manchu troops, bringing the total to three thousand.

sentences.zh: 及道光六年，那彥成奏請裁撤海口官兵，改歸大名鎮。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Daoguang, Nayancheng memorialized to abolish harbor-mouth troops and officers and transfer them to Daming garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 6 (1826), Nayancheng proposed abolishing the harbor garrison and assigning the men to Daming.

sentences.zh: 十二年，琦善奏天津地處海隅，與山東登州、奉天錦州遙相拱衛，沙線分歧，非熟習海徑者，無由曲折而至。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Qishan memorialized that Tianjin lay on the sea corner, remotely bracketed with Shandong's Dengzhou and Fengtian's Jinzhou; sandbars branched apart, and without mastery of sea routes one could not reach it by winding paths.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12 (1832), Qishan argued that Tianjin, flanked from afar by Dengzhou and Jinzhou, was shielded by branching sandbars that only mariners who knew the channels could thread.

sentences.zh: 且海口二十里外，有攔港沙一道，融結天成，儼若海口外衛。

translations.literal: Moreover, twenty li outside the harbor mouth there was a barrier-sand bar formed by natural fusion, like an outer guard for the harbor mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li offshore a natural sand barrier had formed, serving almost as an outer rampart for the harbor.

sentences.zh: 總兵陸路營伍，足資捍衛，所有天津水師，無庸復設。

translations.literal: The regional commander's land camps were sufficient for defense; the entire Tianjin naval force need not be re-established.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander's land forces were defense enough; Tianjin needed no naval battalion again.

sentences.zh: 於是水師營遂裁。

translations.literal: Thereupon the naval battalion was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The naval battalion was duly disbanded.

sentences.zh: 二十年，又據琦善奏英艦到粵，難保不分投竄擾，天津密邇京畿，尤宜慎重防堵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, again based on Qishan's memorial that British ships had reached Guangdong and might not fail to detach forces to raid elsewhere, Tianjin was close to the capital region and especially should be carefully blocked and defended.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 20 (1840), Qishan warned that with British ships at Guangdong they might strike elsewhere, and Tianjin—hard by the capital—must be sealed with special care.

sentences.zh: 遂復嚴旨派員駐紮要隘，協同防禦。

translations.literal: Thereupon a strict edict again dispatched officers to garrison key passes and cooperate in defense.
translations.idiomatic: An urgent order again posted officers at critical points for joint defense.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，天津海口增駐官兵，建砲台營房，近海村落，招集團練，修築土堡，互為策應。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, at Tianjin harbor troops and officers were increased; fort barracks were built; in villages near the sea militia were recruited, earthen forts constructed, mutually supporting one another.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 (1841) more troops were posted at Tianjin harbor, forts and barracks built, and coastal villages mustered into militia with earthen forts that could support one another.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，令直隸沿海營兵，善於鳧水及諳習風濤駕駛之技者，飭統兵官訓練，並增設巡哨兵船，以蘆台為北塘後路，設通永鎮標十五營駐守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, among Zhili's coastal garrison troops those skilled at swimming and versed in navigating wind and waves were ordered trained by commanding officers; patrol gunboats were also added; with Lutai as Beitang's rear route, fifteen battalions of the Tongyong garrison standard were set to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 22 (1842), among Zhili's coastal garrison troops, those skilled at swimming and familiar with wind, waves, and piloting were ordered to be trained by the commanding officers. Patrol boats were also added, Lutai was made Beitang's rear route, and fifteen battalions of the Tongyong garrison standard were stationed there.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，令天津水師營每年撥戰船六艘，分三路巡防，與奉天、山東師船，定期會哨，以登州、岫岩城、錦州三處為呈票考驗之地。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the Tianjin naval battalion was ordered to allocate six warships yearly, patrolling in three routes, meeting Fengtian and Shandong naval vessels on schedule; Dengzhou, Xiuyan city, and Jinzhou were places for presenting tickets and inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 23 (1843) Tianjin was to deploy six warships yearly on three patrol routes, rendezvous with Fengtian and Shandong flotillas, and report at Dengzhou, Xiuyan, and Jinzhou for inspection.

sentences.zh: 有畏避風浪，巡哨貽誤者，嚴懲之。

translations.literal: Those who feared wind and waves and delayed patrol were severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: Officers who shirked rough weather and missed patrol faced severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 三十年，令訥爾經額察視海防。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Ne'erjing'e was ordered to inspect coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 30 (1850), Ne'erjing'e was sent to inspect the coast.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，令僧格林沁在大沽口及雙港修築砲台，設水路木筏，及沿岸營壘，調宣化鎮兵會大沽協兵，守護海口砲台。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, Senggelinqin was ordered to build forts at Dagu mouth and Shuanggang, set up wooden rafts on the waterways and camps along the shore, transfer Xuanhua garrison troops to join Dagu assistant troops, and guard the harbor-mouth forts.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 8 (1858), Senggelinqin built forts at Dagu and Shuanggang, laid wooden booms on the channels, posted shore batteries, and brought Xuanhua troops to reinforce the Dagu garrison defending the forts.

sentences.zh: 又令史榮椿等由天津赴山海關履勘海防要隘。

translations.literal: Shi Rongchun and others were also ordered from Tianjin to Shanhaiguan to survey coastal defense key points on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Rongchun and others were also sent from Tianjin to Shanhaiguan to survey coastal strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，令曾國籓、薛煥等購買外洋兵船巨砲，統以鎮將，酌分數艘，駐泊天津海口。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Zeng Guofan, Xue Huan, and others were ordered to purchase foreign gunboats and heavy cannon; a regional commander unified them; several vessels as appropriate were stationed at Tianjin harbor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 (1862), Zeng Guofan and Xue Huan were told to buy foreign gunboats and heavy guns; a regional commander took charge and several were stationed at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 九年，山東巡撫丁寶楨以大沽、北塘等處為京師門戶，慮直隸兵力不足，調山東舊部十八營，赴直隸邊境候調。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Shandong governor Ding Baozhen, because Dagu, Beitang, and other places were the capital's gateway, fearing Zhili's forces were insufficient, transferred eighteen battalions of his old Shandong command to Zhili's border to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 9 (1870), Shandong governor Ding Baozhen, seeing Dagu and Beitang as the capital's gate and fearing Zhili was under strength, moved eighteen of his old battalions to the Zhili border on standby.

sentences.zh: 十年，直隸總督李鴻章增設大沽協海口六營，酌定營制。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Zhili governor Li Hongzhang added six harbor battalions of the Dagu assistant command and fixed the battalion organization.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 10 (1871), Zhili governor Li Hongzhang added six Dagu harbor battalions and standardized their organization.

sentences.zh: 修築大沽口南北兩岸砲台，與北塘相犄角，調遵化練軍千人移駐。

translations.literal: Forts on both north and south banks of Dagu mouth were built, mutually supporting with Beitang; a thousand men of Zunhua drilled troops were transferred to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Forts rose on both banks of Dagu, paired with Beitang in a pincer, and a thousand Zunhua drilled troops were shifted to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又以北洋海防，僅恃大沽、北塘二海口砲台，後路尚恐單薄，乃就運河北岸，用三合土建築新城，四圍設大小砲台，護以金剛牆，引海河為城濠，屯駐重兵，與大沽防營相應。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, again because Northern Seas coastal defense relied only on the two harbor forts at Dagu and Beitang and the rear route still seemed thin, on the north bank of the canal a new city was built with rammed earth, large and small forts set on all sides, protected by reinforced walls, the Hai River drawn in as moat, heavy troops garrisoned, responding with Dagu's defense camps.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 13 (1874), fearing the Northern Seas defense rested too narrowly on Dagu and Beitang, Li Hongzhang built a new walled city on the canal's north bank with earthen ramparts, ring forts, reinforced walls, the Hai River as moat, and a heavy garrison to back the Dagu line.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，李鴻章復於大沽、北塘、新城各處，增築洋式砲台營壘，購置鐵甲快船、碰船、水雷船，以備攻守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, Li Hongzhang again at Dagu, Beitang, and the new city added Western-style fort camps, purchased ironclad fast cruisers, rams, and mine vessels for offense and defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 1 (1875), Li Hongzhang added Western-style batteries at Dagu, Beitang, and the new city and bought ironclads, rams, and mine craft for both attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 二年，令總兵周盛傳率淮軍馬步二十餘營，建築新城砲台。

translations.literal: In the second year, regional commander Zhou Shengchuan was ordered to lead more than twenty Huai Army cavalry and infantry battalions to build the new city's forts.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 2 (1876), regional commander Zhou Shengchuan led twenty-odd Huai battalions to build the new city's batteries.

sentences.zh: 三年，成之。

translations.literal: In the third year, it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: They were finished in Guangxu 3 (1877).

sentences.zh: 六年，李鴻章以北塘迤東至山海關，延長數百里，調宋慶、郭松林二軍，分駐沿海蒲河口、秦皇島等處，並增建砲台。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Li Hongzhang, because from Beitang east to Shanhaiguan stretched several hundred li, transferred Song Qing's and Guo Songlin's two armies, distributed to garrison at coastal Puhe mouth, Qinhuangdao, and other places, and also added forts.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 (1880), Li Hongzhang posted Song Qing's and Guo Songlin's armies along the hundred-odd li from Beitang to Shanhaiguan—at Puhe mouth, Qinhuangdao, and other beaches—and added batteries.

sentences.zh: 又以淮、練各軍駐天津，防守大沽、北塘各口。

translations.literal: Huai and drilled troops were again stationed at Tianjin to defend Dagu, Beitang, and other mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Huai and drilled units garrisoned Tianjin to hold Dagu and Beitang.

sentences.zh: 以鮑超全軍三十營駐昌黎、樂亭，防守大清河、洋河各口。

translations.literal: Bao Chao's entire army of thirty battalions garrisoned Changli and Leting, defending the mouths of the Daqing and Yang rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chao's thirty battalions held Changli and Leting to cover the Daqing and Yang river mouths.

sentences.zh: 以山海關防軍，兼顧金山嘴、秦皇島、老龍頭各處。

translations.literal: Shanhaiguan defense troops also covered Jinshanzui, Qinhuangdao, Laolongtou, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Shanhaiguan troops also watched Jinshanzui, Qinhuangdao, and Laolongtou.

sentences.zh: 時曾國荃建議直隸海防，不宜遠守營口，宜以重兵守山海關。

translations.literal: At that time Zeng Guoquan proposed that Zhili coastal defense should not guard Yingkou from afar but should hold Shanhaiguan with heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan then urged that Zhili should not spread forces to distant Yingkou but mass troops at Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 乃命曾國荃統率安徽、湖北、山西各軍赴山海關駐守。

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan was then ordered to command armies from Anhui, Hubei, and Shanxi to garrison at Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan was ordered to take Anhui, Hubei, and Shanxi forces to garrison Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 八年，李鴻章於大沽、北塘砲台下埋伏水雷，大沽口內設攔河木筏，山海關內外築三合土大砲台一，土砲台二，瀕海營牆，均仿砲台建築。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Li Hongzhang laid mines under the Dagu and Beitang forts, set blocking rafts inside Dagu mouth, built one large rammed-earth fort and two earthen forts inside and outside Shanhaiguan, and seaside camp walls all modeled on fort construction.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8 (1882), Li Hongzhang mined the Dagu and Beitang batteries, boomed Dagu's inner channel, and built one major and two subsidiary earthen forts at Shanhaiguan, with seaside walls cast in the fort style.

sentences.zh: 又寧海城臨海受敵，於砲台牆外，悉以沙土掩護。

translations.literal: Ninghai city also faced the sea and enemy attack; outside the fort walls everything was covered with sand and earth for protection.
translations.idiomatic: At exposed Ninghai, sand and earth were heaped over the batteries for added protection.

sentences.zh: 其時大沽南北岸砲台大小共數十座，輔以水雷鐵艦，沿岸以陸軍駐守。

translations.literal: At that time on Dagu's north and south banks there were several dozen large and small forts, assisted by mines and ironclads, with land forces garrisoned along the coast.
translations.idiomatic: By then Dagu's shores held dozens of batteries, backed by mines and ironclads and a coastal cordon of infantry.

sentences.zh: 十一年，因京東沿海空虛，調練軍各營，移駐灤州、昌黎等處。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, because the capital's eastern coast was empty, drilled-army battalions were transferred to garrison at Luanzhou, Changli, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 11 (1885), drilled battalions filled the thinly held Jingdong coast at Luanzhou, Changli, and nearby posts.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，直隸總督王文韶以武毅軍訓練初成，率前後二軍及馬隊一軍，周曆山海關沿海一帶，以重防務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Zhili governor Wang Wenshao, because the Wuyi Army's training was newly complete, led its front and rear armies and one cavalry army on a circuit of the Shanhaiguan coastal strip to strengthen defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 23 (1897), Zhili governor Wang Wenshao, with the newly trained Wuyi Army, toured the Shanhaiguan coast with its two infantry wings and cavalry brigade to tighten defenses.

sentences.zh: 自歐艦來窺，僧格林沁戰敗，廷議始專津、沽之防。

translations.literal: From the time European ships came to reconnoiter and Senggelinqin was defeated, court debate began to focus defense on Tianjin and Dagu.
translations.idiomatic: After European squadrons probed the coast and Senggelinqin was beaten, the court fixed its attention on Tianjin and Dagu.

sentences.zh: 中日之役，旅順、威海相繼淪陷，而津海未開戰事。

translations.literal: In the Sino-Japanese War, Lüshun and Weihai fell in succession, yet the Tianjin sea saw no fighting.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sino-Japanese War, Lüshun and Weihai fell in turn, but Tianjin's waters never saw battle.

sentences.zh: 及拳匪肇釁，聯軍北犯，沽口砲台，毀於一旦，北洋沿海防務，遂日形懈弛雲。

translations.literal: When the Boxers provoked trouble and the allied armies invaded north, the Dagu forts were destroyed in a day, and Northern Seas coastal defense daily grew slack.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer rising brought the allied armies north, Dagu's forts were smashed overnight and Beiyang coastal defense sank into steady decay.

sentences.zh: 山東海岸綿亙，自直隸界屈曲而南以達江蘇，其間大小海口二百餘處。

translations.literal: Shandong's coast stretched continuously, from the Zhili border winding south to Jiangsu, with more than two hundred large and small harbors between.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's shoreline ran from the Zhili border south to Jiangsu in a long curve, with more than two hundred harbors along it.

sentences.zh: 東北境之登、萊、青三府，地形突出，三面臨海。

translations.literal: In the northeast of the province the three prefectures Deng, Lai, and Qing had terrain projecting outward, facing the sea on three sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the province's northeast, Dengzhou, Laizhou, and Qingzhou jutted into the sea on three sides.

sentences.zh: 威海、煙台島嶼環羅，與朝鮮海峽對峙，為幽、薊屏籓。

translations.literal: Weihai and Yantai were ringed with islands, facing the Korea Strait, serving as the protective screen for You and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Weihai and Yantai, ringed with islands opposite the Korea Strait, formed the maritime shield for the capital region.

sentences.zh: 海禁既開，各國商帆戰艦，歷重洋而來，至山東成山而折入渤海，以達沽口。

translations.literal: Once the maritime ban was lifted, merchant sails and warships of all nations came across the great ocean, reaching Shandong's Chengshan and turning into the Bohai to reach Dagu mouth.
translations.idiomatic: With trade opened, foreign merchantmen and warships crossed the oceans to Chengshan Cape, turned into the Bohai, and made for Dagu.

sentences.zh: 故創練海軍，以威海、旅順為根據地。

translations.literal: Therefore in creating and drilling the navy, Weihai and Lüshun were taken as base areas.
translations.idiomatic: The modern navy was therefore based at Weihai and Lüshun.

sentences.zh: 欲守津、沽，先守威、旅。

translations.literal: To defend Tianjin and Dagu, one must first defend Weihai and Lüshun.
translations.idiomatic: To hold Tianjin and Dagu, one had to hold Weihai and Lüshun first.

sentences.zh: 齊、魯關山，遂與畿疆並重矣。

translations.literal: Qi and Lu's mountain passes thus became as weighty as the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's passes thus rose to equal importance with the capital district itself.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，令蘇利為水軍都督，駐軍碣石，為山東防海之始。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi, Suli was appointed naval commander-in-chief, troops garrisoned at Jieshi—the beginning of Shandong's sea defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 (1654), Suli was made naval commander with a garrison at Jieshi, marking the start of Shandong's coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十五年，以膠州、文登、即墨等營，兼防海口，以總兵駐登州，統水師三營，戰船十二艘，修治各海口砲台。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong, Jiaozhou, Wendeng, Jimo, and other garrisons also guarded harbor mouths; a regional commander garrisoned at Dengzhou commanded three naval battalions and twelve warships, repairing forts at each harbor mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 55 (1790), Jiaozhou, Wendeng, and Jimo garrisons took on harbor defense; a regional commander at Dengzhou led three naval battalions and twelve warships and repaired the coastal batteries.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年，以芝罘島扼東海之口，撥兵防守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang, because Zhifu Island commanded the mouth of the Eastern Sea, troops were allocated for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 (1841), troops were posted to Zhifu Island, which commands the Eastern Sea entrance.

sentences.zh: 蓬萊、黃縣、榮城、寧海、掖縣、膠州、即墨所屬之十三島，編練民團，互為防衛。

translations.literal: The thirteen islands belonging to Penglai, Huangxian, Rongcheng, Ninghai, Yexian, Jiaozhou, and Jimo had militia organized and drilled for mutual defense.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteen islands under Penglai, Huangxian, Rongcheng, Ninghai, Yexian, Jiaozhou, and Jimo, militia were organized to defend one another.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以瀕海之三汛師船，四縣水勇，合併防守海口，並扼要安設大砲。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, coastal patrol vessels on three routes and water braves from four counties were combined to defend harbor mouths, and heavy guns were installed at strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 30 (1850), coastal patrol craft on three routes and water militia from four counties were pooled to hold the harbors, with heavy guns emplaced at key points.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，登州總兵陳世忠以海寇奪掠官船，山東水師無多，會閩、粵大號師船，合力截捕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, Dengzhou regional commander Chen Shizhong, because sea bandits seized and plundered official vessels and Shandong's naval force was not large, joined large warships from Fujian and Guangdong to intercept and capture them together.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 1 (1851), when sea pirates seized official vessels, Dengzhou commander Chen Shizhong—finding Shandong's fleet too thin—combined with large Fujian and Guangdong warships to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 三年，於登、萊、青三府舉辦聯庄團練，給以兵械。

translations.literal: In the third year, in the three prefectures Deng, Lai, and Qing linked-village militia training was organized, and they were supplied with weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 (1853), linked-village militia were raised in Dengzhou, Laizhou, and Qingzhou and issued arms.

sentences.zh: 八年，飭天津鎮總兵赴山東，詳勘海豐一帶海口。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Tianjin garrison regional commander was ordered to go to Shandong and conduct a detailed survey of harbor mouths in the Haifeng region.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 8 (1858), the Tianjin garrison commander was sent to Shandong to survey the Haifeng coastal harbors in detail.

sentences.zh: 九年，以海豐縣之大沽河有防營故址，飭崇恩等撥兵防守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because Haifeng County's Dagu River had the site of a former defense camp, Chong'en and others were ordered to allocate troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 9 (1859), troops under Chong'en and others were posted to the old garrison site on the Dagu River in Haifeng County.

sentences.zh: 十年，文煜令青州等沿海各城滿、綠營兵，勤加訓練，分守城官兵之半以守海口。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Wen Yu ordered Manchu and Green Standard troops in coastal cities such as Qingzhou to train diligently, and half the garrison troops were divided off to defend harbor mouths.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 (1860), Wen Yu had Manchu and Green Standard garrisons in Qingzhou and other coastal cities drill hard, detaching half their strength to hold the harbors.

sentences.zh: 同治九年，丁寶楨以東境海口紛歧，惟有扼要防守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tongzhi, Ding Baozhen, because eastern harbor mouths were numerous and divergent, held that one could only defend by seizing strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 9 (1870), Ding Baozhen argued that with so many eastern harbors, defense had to concentrate on choke points.

sentences.zh: 其文登縣屬之馬頭石島，福山縣屬之煙台，蓬萊縣屬之廟島，掖縣屬之小石島，為洋船北來所必經，第居險要，共撥兵六千餘人分守。

translations.literal: Matou Rock Island under Wendeng County, Yantai under Fushan County, Miaodao under Penglai County, and Xiaoshi Island under Yexian County were routes foreign ships coming north must pass; occupying strategic positions, more than six thousand troops were allocated in divided garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Matou Rock Island (Wendeng), Yantai (Fushan), Miaodao (Penglai), and Xiaoshi Island (Yexian) lay on the northbound lane of foreign shipping; more than six thousand men were posted to these key points.

sentences.zh: 十一年，撥大號兵船一艘，駐泊登州洋面。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, one large warship was allocated and stationed on the open sea off Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 11 (1872), a large warship was posted off Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，丁寶楨以山東之東三府，三面環海，外寇隨處可登，宜扼要屯守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, Ding Baozhen, because Shandong's eastern three prefectures were ringed by sea on three sides and foreign invaders could land anywhere, held that one should garrison at strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 1 (1875), Ding Baozhen urged key garrisons for Shandong's eastern trio—Deng, Lai, and Qing—which faced the sea on three sides and offered landing sites everywhere.

sentences.zh: 其要地有三：一、煙台，於通申岡設防營，駐兵三千。

translations.literal: The key places were three: first, Yantai—at Tongshen Hill a defense camp was set up, garrisoning three thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Three positions mattered most: Yantai, where a fort was placed on Tongshen Hill with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 煙台山下及八蜡廟、芝罘島之西，共建浮鐵砲台三座。

translations.literal: Below Yantai Mountain and at Balao Temple and west of Zhifu Island, three floating iron batteries were built together.
translations.idiomatic: Three floating iron batteries were erected below Yantai Hill, at Balao Temple, and west of Zhifu Island.

sentences.zh: 芝罘島之東，築沙土曲折砲台一座。

translations.literal: East of Zhifu Island, one earthen zigzag battery was built.
translations.idiomatic: East of Zhifu Island they built an earthen zigzag battery.

sentences.zh: 一、威海衛，於劉公島之東口，建浮鐵砲台一座，而於島口內築沙土曲折砲台，於口外海面密布水雷，其北口內亦建沙土浮鐵砲台，可作兵輪船水寨之用。

translations.literal: Second, Weihaiwei—at the eastern mouth of Liugong Island one floating iron battery was built, while within the island mouth an earthen zigzag battery was constructed; outside the mouth on the sea surface naval mines were densely laid; within the northern mouth as well a sand-and-iron floating battery was built, usable as a steam-warship naval stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Second, Weihaiwei: a floating iron battery at Liugong Island's east entrance, an earthen zigzag battery inside the channel, mines thick in the outer roadstead, and another combined sand-and-iron battery in the north entrance that could serve as a steam-fleet anchorage.

sentences.zh: 一、登州，於城北建沙土高式砲台，城內建沙土圓式砲台。

translations.literal: Third, Dengzhou—north of the city an earthen high-style battery was built, and within the city an earthen round-style battery.
translations.idiomatic: Third, Dengzhou: a tall earthen battery north of the walls and a round earthen battery within the city.

sentences.zh: 長山之西，建沙土曲折砲台，與郡城相犄角。

translations.literal: West of Changshan, an earthen zigzag battery was built, forming a pincer with the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: West of Changshan an earthen zigzag battery was added to flank the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 砲台用克魯伯後膛大砲，參用阿姆司脫朗前膛大砲。

translations.literal: The batteries used Krupp breech-loading heavy guns, supplemented with Armstrong muzzle-loading heavy guns.
translations.idiomatic: Batteries mounted Krupp breech-loaders, with Armstrong muzzle-loaders in support.

sentences.zh: 兵丁用格林砲、克魯伯四磅砲、亨利馬悌尼快槍，請求行陣攻守之法。

translations.literal: The soldiers used Gatling guns, Krupp four-pounders, and Henry-Martini rapid-fire rifles, and requested instruction in battlefield offensive and defensive methods.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were issued Gatling guns, Krupp four-pounders, and Henry-Martini rifles, and drilled in field attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 六年，以新購外洋蚊砲船駐防煙台海面。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, newly purchased foreign gunboats were stationed to defend the Yantai sea surface.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 (1880), newly bought foreign gunboats were posted off Yantai.

sentences.zh: 十二年，許景澄建議山東膠州灣當南北洋之中，東為浮山，西為靈山，口狹而水深，宜規畫形勢，為新練海軍屯港，與旅順口東西相應。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Xu Jingcheng proposed that Shandong's Jiaozhou Bay stood between the northern and southern seas, with Fushan to the east and Lingshan to the west, the mouth narrow and the water deep—it was suitable to plan the terrain as a naval anchorage for the newly drilled navy, corresponding east and west with Lüshunkou.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 12 (1886), Xu Jingcheng urged developing Jiaozhou Bay—midway between northern and southern waters, Fushan east and Lingshan west, narrow mouth and deep channel—as a base for the new navy, paired with Lüshun across the gulf.

sentences.zh: 是年，李鴻章於威海衛南北岸築砲台，布水雷。

translations.literal: That year, Li Hongzhang built batteries on Weihaiwei's north and south shores and laid naval mines.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Hongzhang fortified both shores of Weihaiwei and seeded the waters with mines.

sentences.zh: 十七年，於威海黃泥岩增築新式砲台，又於南岸龍廟嘴砲台外，增築趙北口砲台。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, at Weihai's Huangniyan newly styled batteries were added, and south of the shore at Longmiaozui Battery, Zhaobeikou Battery was additionally built.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 17 (1891), new batteries rose at Weihai's Huangniyan, and Zhaobeikou Battery was added beyond Longmiaozui on the south shore.

sentences.zh: 劉公島新築地阱砲台，設後膛巨砲於隧道。

translations.literal: On Liugong Island a new sunken battery was built, with breech-loading giant guns set in tunnels.
translations.idiomatic: Liugong Island gained a sunken battery with huge breech-loaders mounted in tunnels.

sentences.zh: 其西之黃島，水中之日島，亦設砲台，與南岸相應。

translations.literal: Huangdao to its west and Ri Island in the water also had batteries installed, corresponding with the south shore.
translations.idiomatic: Batteries on Huangdao to the west and Ri Island in the channel complemented the south shore defenses.

sentences.zh: 劉公島又設大鐵碼頭，為海軍寄椗上煤之所，防務益周密。

translations.literal: Liugong Island also had a large iron pier set up, serving as a place for the navy to moor and take on coal, and coastal defense grew more thorough.
translations.idiomatic: A large iron pier on Liugong Island gave the fleet a coaling station, tightening the defenses further.

sentences.zh: 東省形勢，以威海、膠州為要口，于海軍屯泊尤宜。

translations.literal: The terrain of the eastern province took Weihai and Jiaozhou as key mouths, especially suitable for naval anchorage.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's geography made Weihai and Jiaozhou the prime anchorages for fleet deployment.

sentences.zh: 乃甲午一役，威海水陸之防，既毀於日本，而德因教案，曾以大隊鐵艦奪踞膠州灣，辟商埠，開鐵路，浸窺腹地。

translations.literal: But in the war of Jiawu, Weihai's land and sea defenses were destroyed by Japan; and Germany, because of the missionary case, once with a large force of ironclads seized and occupied Jiaozhou Bay, opened a commercial port, built railways, and gradually peered into the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the war of 1894–95 smashed Weihai's defenses, and Germany later seized Jiaozhou Bay with a squadron of ironclads over the missionary affair—opening a treaty port, laying rail, and probing the interior.

sentences.zh: 東省海防，遂無所藉手雲。

translations.literal: Shandong's coastal defense thus had nothing to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's coastal defense was left with no firm ground to stand on.

sentences.zh: 江南海防，自海州南歷長江、吳淞江二口，稍折而西，至松江奉賢縣境之海灣，南接浙江洋面，其間港口羅列。

translations.literal: Jiangnan's coastal defense, from Haizhou south passing the Yangtze and Wusong River mouths, turning slightly west to the bay at Fengxian County in Songjiang, joining Zhejiang's sea surface to the south—with harbors arrayed between.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan's coast ran south from Haizhou past the Yangtze and Wusong entries, then westward to Fengxian Bay in Songjiang and the Zhejiang sea beyond, harbors strung all along.

sentences.zh: 惟江陰、吳淞二處，一為長江之筦鍵，一為蘇、松之門戶，防務尤重。

translations.literal: Only at Jiangyin and Wusong—the one the Yangtze's gateway, the other the portal of Suzhou and Songjiang—coastal defense was especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin and Wusong bore the heaviest burden: one guarded the Yangtze's throat, the other the gateway to Suzhou and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 至江陰以上，以江流深廣，外海兵艦商船，溯流而上，西達夔、渝，三千里流域，雖皖、贛、楚、蜀各有江防，實以江南當下游之沖。

translations.literal: Above Jiangyin, because the river flow was deep and broad, foreign warships and merchant vessels from the open sea could ascend upstream west to Kuizhou and Chongqing—a three-thousand-li watershed; although Anhui, Jiangxi, Hubei, and Sichuan each had river defense, in truth Jiangnan bore the brunt of the lower reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Upriver from Jiangyin the channel runs deep and wide; oceangoing warships and merchantmen can sail three thousand li to Chongqing. Each upstream province had its own river guard, but Jiangnan held the lower Yangtze's front line.

sentences.zh: 自狼、福山以迄京口、金陵，砲壘防營，星羅棋布。

translations.literal: From Lang and Fushan to Jingkou and Jinling, gun fortifications and defense camps were scattered like stars in a chessboard.
translations.idiomatic: From Langshan and Fushan to Jingkou and Nanjing, batteries and garrison posts dotted the banks like a constellation.

sentences.zh: 上游防衛，與下游繁簡迥殊。

translations.literal: Upstream defense and downstream—in their complexity and simplicity—differed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Upstream and downstream defenses differed sharply in scale and detail.

sentences.zh: 而江蘇轄境，長江千里，兵艦砲台，無異海防，水陸營汛，亦與海疆聯絡。

translations.literal: Yet within Jiangsu's jurisdiction, the Yangtze for a thousand li—with warships and batteries no different from sea defense—land and water garrison posts also linked with the maritime frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Within Jiangsu the thousand-li Yangtze was defended like a coast: gunboats, batteries, and linked land-and-water patrol posts tied the river line to the sea frontier.

sentences.zh: 故安徽省以上江防，即隸於蘇省海防焉。

translations.literal: Therefore river defense above Anhui Province was subordinate to Jiangsu Province's coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: River defense upstream of Anhui thus fell under Jiangsu's coastal command.

sentences.zh: 自海州南抵江口，乃昔年黃河入海處，泥沙積久，凝結內海，稱五條沙，海潮甚急。

translations.literal: From Haizhou south to the river mouth was where the Yellow River once entered the sea; silt accumulated over long years and coalesced into an inner sea called the Five Bars, with very swift tides.
translations.idiomatic: From Haizhou south to the river mouth lay the old Yellow River delta, where silt had built the Five Bars shoals and the tides ran fierce.

sentences.zh: 海舶北赴燕、齊者，必東行一晝夜以避其沙，故淮、海州郡，得稍寬海防者，以五條沙為之保障也。

translations.literal: Sea vessels heading north to Yan and Qi had to sail east one day and one night to avoid its sand; thus the Huai and Haizhou districts could leave coastal defense somewhat relaxed—the Five Bars serving as their protection.
translations.idiomatic: Northbound shipping for Yan and Qi had to detour east a full day to clear the shoals, which gave Huai and Haizhou a natural screen and eased their coastal burden.

sentences.zh: 自狼、福山口南抵吳淞，沙凝潮急，略同北境。

translations.literal: From the mouths of Lang and Fushan south to Wusong, sand congealed and tides swift—roughly the same as the northern sector.
translations.idiomatic: From Langshan and Fushan south to Wusong, shoals and rushing tides resembled the northern coast.

sentences.zh: 惟長江、吳淞二口，水深溜大，巨艦可直駛內江，故海口防務，視海濱倍重。

translations.literal: Only at the Yangtze and Wusong mouths the water was deep and the current strong; giant ships could sail straight into the inner river—therefore harbor-mouth defense was twice as heavy as along the shore.
translations.idiomatic: But the Yangtze and Wusong entries ran deep with a powerful current, admitting heavy ships directly upriver—so harbor defense there weighed twice the open coast.

sentences.zh: 清初平定江南，分八旗勁旅駐京口，以鎮海大將軍統之，設水師營，造沙唬船以習水戰。

translations.literal: Early in the Qing, after pacifying Jiangnan, elite Eight Banner forces were stationed at Jingkou under the Naval Commander-in-Chief; a naval battalion was established and sand-junks built to practice water combat.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qing pacified Jiangnan, elite Banner troops garrisoned Jingkou under the Naval Commander-in-Chief; a river fleet of sand-junks was raised for training.

sentences.zh: 旋以沙唬船難涉大洋，乃改造鳥船。

translations.literal: Soon, because sand-junks had difficulty crossing the great ocean, bird boats were rebuilt instead.
translations.idiomatic: Sand-junks proving unfit for open sea, the fleet was converted to bird boats.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功據台灣，以師船進窺江表，由京口薄金陵，梁化鳳擊敗之。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Chenggong held Taiwan and sent warships to probe Jiangnan; from Jingkou they pressed on Nanjing, and Liang Huafeng defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Chenggong held Taiwan and sent warships to probe the lower Yangtze, pressing from Jingkou toward Nanjing, Liang Huafeng drove them off.

sentences.zh: 順治十四年，命梁化鳳為水軍都督，率軍萬人，駐防崇明、吳淞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi, Liang Huafeng was appointed naval commander-in-chief, leading ten thousand troops garrisoned at Chongming and Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 14 (1657), Liang Huafeng was made naval commander with ten thousand men at Chongming and Wusong.

sentences.zh: 以松江府三面臨海，設提督，駐重兵。

translations.literal: Because Songjiang Prefecture faced the sea on three sides, a provincial military commander was established and heavy troops garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Songjiang Prefecture, exposed to the sea on three sides, received a provincial commander and a heavy garrison.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，因崇明孤懸大海，嚴出海之禁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, because Chongming stood isolated in the great sea, the ban on going to sea was strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 (1667), Chongming's isolation in open water prompted a strict ban on seagoing.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以提督統八營駐崇明。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the provincial commander commanded eight battalions garrisoned at Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 (1675), the provincial commander took eight battalions to Chongming.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，減存四營，列汛六十有八。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, reduced to four remaining battalions, with sixty-eight patrol posts listed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23 (1684), the force was cut to four battalions manning sixty-eight patrol posts.

sentences.zh: 太倉州為元代海運放洋之口，明代置兵屯守，清初設游擊，以劉河營移駐茜涇鎮。

translations.literal: Taicang Prefecture was the Yuan dynasty's port for ocean-going grain transport; in the Ming troops were stationed; early Qing a battalion commander was established, and the Liuhe Battalion was moved to garrison Qianjing Town.
translations.idiomatic: Taicang, the Yuan grain-fleet sailing port, had been garrisoned since Ming times; early Qing posted a battalion commander there and moved the Liuhe Battalion to Qianjing.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，分設寶山縣，列汛五十有七。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, Baoshan County was separately established, with fifty-seven patrol posts listed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 (1726), Baoshan County was carved out with fifty-seven patrol posts.

sentences.zh: 上海縣當黃浦江之沖，原有墩台十七座，康熙二年，以墩台距海較遠，乃建外塘斥堠。

translations.literal: Shanghai County stood at the convergence of the Huangpu River; originally there were seventeen blockhouses; in the second year of Kangxi, because the blockhouses were relatively far from the sea, outer-shore watch beacons were built.
translations.idiomatic: Shanghai County at the Huangpu's mouth had seventeen blockhouses; in Kangxi 2 (1663), because they sat too far inland, outer-shore watch beacons were added.

sentences.zh: 其南為金山縣，踞青浦、南匯之上游，設參將駐守，列汛七十有八。

translations.literal: To its south was Jinshan county, occupying the upper reaches of Qingpu and Nanhui; a deputy regional commander was stationed there, with seventy-eight patrol posts established.
translations.idiomatic: South lay Jinshan County, upstream of Qingpu and Nanhui, garrisoned by a deputy regional commander and seventy-eight patrol posts.

sentences.zh: 常熟之福山，與隔江之狼山對峙，常熟、昭文瀕海之口，為許浦、徐陸涇、白第港，康熙間，設墩堡戍守，列汛二十有四。

translations.literal: Fushan of Changshu faced Langshan across the river; the sea-facing mouths of Changshu and Zhaowen were Xupu, Xulu Jing, and Baidi Harbor; during the Kangxi era blockhouses were set for garrison, with twenty-four patrol posts established.
translations.idiomatic: Fushan in Changshu stood opposite Langshan across the river. The coastal openings of Changshu and Zhaowen were Xupu, Xulu Creek, and Baidi Harbor; in the Kangxi reign blockhouses were manned, with twenty-four patrol posts.

sentences.zh: 通州為狼山營汛地，如皋為掘港營汛地，皆近海要區也。

translations.literal: Tongzhou was the garrison territory of the Langshan battalion; Rugao was the garrison territory of the Juegang battalion—both were important coastal zones.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou fell under the Langshan battalion's posts and Rugao under the Juegang battalion's—both vital coastal sectors.

sentences.zh: 其北境之海州，為南北襟要，海口之大者凡九，最北為荻水口，其東北雲台山，清初曾徙民內地，阻塞入海之道，康熙二十年復開通，設通海營，列汛五十有五。

translations.literal: Haizhou on its northern border was a strategic hinge between north and south; there were nine major harbor mouths in all, northernmost being Dishui Mouth; to its northeast was Yuntai Mountain—at the beginning of the Qing the people were relocated inland, blocking the route to the sea; in the twentieth year of Kangxi it was reopened, the Tonghai battalion established, and fifty-five patrol posts set.
translations.idiomatic: North lay Haizhou, a strategic hinge between north and south, with nine major harbor mouths—the northernmost at Dishui. Northeast rose Yuntai Mountain; early in the dynasty its populace had been moved inland, sealing the sea route until Kangxi 20 (1681), when it was reopened, a Tonghai battalion posted, and fifty-five patrol stations laid out.

sentences.zh: 淮安府昔為淮河入海之處，設廟灣、鹽城二營，會哨巡防，列汛四十有二。

translations.literal: Huaian prefecture was formerly where the Huai River entered the sea; the Miaowan and Yancheng battalions were established, conducting joint patrols for defense, with forty-two patrol posts.
translations.idiomatic: Huaian, where the Huai once reached the sea, had Miaowan and Yancheng battalions that patrolled together, with forty-two posts along the coast.

sentences.zh: 揚州府北之興化，南之泰州，為濱海之縣，清初設守備，康熙十一年，設游擊鎮之，列汛凡十。

translations.literal: Xinghua to the north of Yangzhou prefecture and Taizhou to the south were coastal counties; at the beginning of the Qing a garrison commander was set; in the eleventh year of Kangxi a brigade commander was stationed there; ten patrol posts in all.
translations.idiomatic: Xinghua north of Yangzhou and Taizhou south of it were coastal counties. Early in the dynasty a garrison commander was posted; in Kangxi 11 (1672) a brigade commander took command, with ten patrol posts.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，以福山營為江海門戶，於江蘇鎮標四營內分兵船二艘隸之，與狼山營會哨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, because the Fushan battalion was the gateway between river and sea, two troop ships were detached from the four battalions of the Jiangsu garrison standard and assigned to it, joint-patrolling with the Langshan battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 (1730), Fushan being the river's gate to the sea, two gunboats were detached from Jiangsu's four garrison battalions and assigned to it for joint patrol with Langshan.

sentences.zh: 此清初至雍正年江南之海防也。

translations.literal: This was Jiangnan's coastal defense from the beginning of the Qing through the Yongzheng era.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Jiangnan's coastal defense from the early Qing through Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 乾隆至道光，江海清平，防汛率循舊制。

translations.literal: From Qianlong to Daoguang, the rivers and sea were calm; coastal garrison defense generally followed the old system.
translations.idiomatic: From Qianlong through Daoguang the rivers and sea stayed quiet, and coastal garrisons mostly kept to the old arrangements.

sentences.zh: 及道光中葉，海警驟起，東南戒嚴。

translations.literal: By the middle of the Daoguang era, maritime alarms suddenly arose, and the southeast was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Daoguang, maritime alarms flared and the southeast went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以寶山海口為江南要區，屯駐大營，分設游緝之兵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Baoshan harbor mouth was regarded as a key zone of Jiangnan; a major camp was encamped, and patrol-and-suppression troops were separately deployed.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 (1841), Baoshan harbor was deemed a Jiangnan strongpoint; a headquarters camp was posted and patrol troops distributed.

sentences.zh: 吳淞亦屯兵，增設濠壘。

translations.literal: Wusong also encamped troops and added moats and ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Wusong likewise received troops and new entrenchments.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，令耆英等周曆吳淞、狼山、福山、圌山關各處，整頓戰船砲械。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Qiying and others were ordered to tour Wusong, Langshan, Fushan, and Mt. Tu pass and other places, restoring warships and artillery.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 22 (1842), Qiying and others were sent to inspect Wusong, Langshan, Fushan, and Mt. Tu, overhauling warships and guns.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以江陰鵝鼻嘴為由海入江要口，設險守御。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Jiangyin's Ebizu mouth was regarded as the key opening from sea into river; defenses were set at strategic points for protection.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 23 (1843), Jiangyin's Ebizu Point, the chief ingress from sea to river, was fortified at every strong position.

sentences.zh: 又防堵瓜洲及南河、灌河、射陽湖之口。

translations.literal: Guazhou and the mouths of the Nan River, Guan River, and Sheyang Lake were also blocked and defended.
translations.idiomatic: Guazhou and the mouths of the Nan, Guan, and Sheyang Lake were sealed as well.

sentences.zh: 令璧昌等察沿海城邑，聯絡保障。

translations.literal: Bi Chang and others were ordered to inspect coastal cities and towns and coordinate their protection.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Chang and others were dispatched to inspect coastal towns and knit their defenses together.

sentences.zh: 所用砲位，設局開鑄，並造水師舢板船，築砲台於江岸南北。

translations.literal: Artillery needed was cast at specially established bureaus; naval sampan gunboats were also built, and forts constructed on both north and south banks of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Foundries were opened to cast guns; naval gunboats built; fortifications raised on both banks of the river.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，璧昌因狼、福山江面太寬，於劉聞沙、東生洲、順江洲、沙圩等處，修築砲堤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, because the river surface at Lang and Fushan was too wide, Bi Chang built gun embankments at Liuwen Sha, Dongsheng Isle, Shunjiang Isle, Shawei, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 (1844), finding the river too wide at Lang and Fushan, Bi Chang built gun embankments at Liuwen Sha, Dongsheng Isle, Shunjiang Isle, Shawei, and similar spots.

sentences.zh: 水師各營，增大小戰船一百三十餘艘，分廠製造。

translations.literal: Each naval battalion added more than a hundred thirty large and small warships, manufactured at separate yards.
translations.idiomatic: Every naval battalion added over 130 warships of various sizes, built at separate yards.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，李星沅籌防泖湖，貯石沈船，增置木牌，並存儲砲位，分佈重兵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Li Xingyuan prepared defenses at Lake Mao: stones stockpiled, ships sunk, wooden booms added, artillery stored, and heavy forces deployed.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 27 (1847), Li Xingyuan fortified Lake Mao with stockpiled stones, scuttled blockships, new wooden booms, stored guns, and a heavy troop concentration.

sentences.zh: 而其時所築砲台，實止因土為堤，且器械窳舊，布置多疏，非特不足御歐洲巨艦，咸豐間，粵寇東下，沿江防戍，咸望風奔靡。

translations.literal: Yet the forts built at that time were really only earthen embankments; moreover the equipment was worn and obsolete, the disposition mostly loose—not only insufficient to resist European great ships, but during Xianfeng when the Cantonese rebels swept east, coastal garrisons along the river all fled at the mere rumor of their approach.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those forts were little more than earthen ramparts, armed with worn gear and loosely arranged—no match for European men-of-war. When the Taiping swept down the Yangtze in Xianfeng, riverside garrisons broke and ran at the first alarm.

sentences.zh: 及湘軍底定東南，軍勢始振。

translations.literal: After the Hunan Army pacified the southeast, military strength began to revive.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Hunan Army secured the southeast, morale and force revived.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，諭薛煥等購西洋兵艦，在上海等要口防守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Xue Huan and others were instructed to purchase Western warships and defend at Shanghai and other key openings.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 (1862), Xue Huan and others were ordered to buy Western warships and hold Shanghai and other key ports.

sentences.zh: 四年，曾國籓於狼山鎮標，每營增造大舢板船二十號，仿紅單船之式，多設砲位，巡緝內洋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Zeng Guofan at the Langshan garrison standard had each battalion add twenty large sampan gunboats, modeled on the red-bristle junk type, with many gun mounts, patrolling the inner seas.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 4 (1865), Zeng Guofan had each Langshan battalion build twenty large gunboat sampans on the red-bristle junk model, heavily armed, to patrol inland waters.

sentences.zh: 海門設綏海營，置大舢板船二十號，酌設兵輪，分防北岸海汊。

translations.literal: At Haimen the Suihai battalion was established, with twenty large sampan gunboats placed, steam warships deployed as appropriate, dividing defense of the north-bank tidal channels.
translations.idiomatic: Haimen gained a Suihai battalion with twenty large gunboat sampans and a modest steam contingent to cover the north shore's tidal inlets.

sentences.zh: 七年，更定內洋水師五營，外洋水師六營之制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the system of five inner-sea naval battalions and six outer-sea naval battalions was revised and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 7 (1868), the five inner-sea and six outer-sea naval battalions were reorganized.

sentences.zh: 以兵輪四艘，分隸蘇松、狼山、福山三鎮總兵，駐防海口。

translations.literal: Four steam warships were separately assigned to the Suzhou-Songjiang, Langshan, and Fushan regional commanders, garrisoning harbor mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Four steamers were apportioned among the Suzhou-Songjiang, Langshan, and Fushan commanders to guard the harbor mouths.

sentences.zh: 九年，南洋初設兵輪統領，駕駛出洋，周曆島嶼。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Southern Seas first established a steam-warship commander, who sailed out to sea and toured the islands.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 9 (1870), the Southern Seas command appointed its first steam flotilla chief, who put to sea and surveyed the islands.

sentences.zh: 十三年，調陝防武毅軍馬步二十二營，赴山東、江南沿海適中之地駐防日本。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, twenty-two cavalry and infantry battalions of the Shaanxi Wuyi Army were transferred to suitable points along the Shandong and Jiangnan coasts to garrison against Japan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 13 (1874), twenty-two battalions of the Shaanxi Wuyi Army were deployed at strategic points on the Shandong and Jiangnan coasts to guard against Japan.

sentences.zh: 時台灣告警，李宗羲以蘇、松之門戶，吳淞為要，長江之關鍵，江陰為先，而鎮江府屬之焦山、象山，對岸之天都廟，江寧府屬之烏龍山，省城外之下關，均為扼要。

translations.literal: At the time Taiwan raised alarms; Li Zongxi regarded Wusong as the gateway of Suzhou and Songjiang, Jiangyin as foremost among the Yangtze's key points, while Jiaoshan and Xiangshan belonging to Zhenjiang prefecture, Tiandu Temple on the opposite bank, Wulong Mountain belonging to Jiangning prefecture, and Xiaguan outside the provincial capital were all strategic choke points.
translations.idiomatic: With Taiwan in crisis, Li Zongxi ranked Wusong as Suzhou-Songjiang's gateway and Jiangyin as the Yangtze's first line; Jiaoshan and Xiangshan in Zhenjiang, Tiandu Temple across the river, Jiangning's Wulong Mountain, and Xiaguan below the provincial capital were all critical holds.

sentences.zh: 以大木方石為基，搗三合土，築砲台砲門，護以鐵柱鐵板，空其下以藏砲兵。

translations.literal: Using large timber and squared stone as foundations, rammed earth was pounded; fort gates and platforms were built, protected with iron pillars and iron plates, the space below hollowed to shelter gun crews.
translations.idiomatic: Foundations were laid in timber and ashlar, walls built of rammed earth, embrasures shielded with iron pillars and plates, the hollow below sheltering gun crews.

sentences.zh: 先築烏龍山砲台十六座，以次江陰、天都廟、象山、焦山、下關各築明暗砲台，置巨砲。

translations.literal: Sixteen forts were first built at Wulong Mountain; then at Jiangyin, Tiandu Temple, Xiangshan, Jiaoshan, and Xiaguan open and concealed forts were built in succession, with great guns emplaced.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen forts went up first at Wulong Mountain, then open and masked batteries at Jiangyin, Tiandu Temple, Xiangshan, Jiaoshan, and Xiaguan, each mounting heavy guns.

sentences.zh: 北岸之沙州圩、吳淞口，及江陰北岸之劉聞沙，亦一律增建砲台，以嚴防務。

translations.literal: Shazhou Wei and Wusong mouth on the north bank, and Liuwen Sha on Jiangyin's north bank, likewise had forts added uniformly, to tighten defense duties.
translations.idiomatic: Shazhou Wei, Wusong mouth, and Liuwen Sha on Jiangyin's north bank likewise received new forts to tighten the cordon.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，劉坤一於江陰鵝鼻嘴砲台外，復於下游增築砲台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, Liu Kunyi beyond the Jiangyin Ebizu fort also added forts downstream.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 1 (1875), Liu Kunyi built additional forts downstream from Jiangyin's Ebizu battery.

sentences.zh: 其北岸之十圩港，亦增築砲台，與南岸相犄角。

translations.literal: At Shiwei Harbor on its north bank forts were also added, mutually supporting with the south bank like horns of a bull.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwei Harbor on the north bank gained forts as well, pinching the river with the south bank.

sentences.zh: 又修改焦山、圌山關、烏龍山等處砲門，以期合法。

translations.literal: Gun embrasures at Jiaoshan, Mt. Tu pass, Wulong Mountain, and other places were also modified to meet proper standards.
translations.idiomatic: Embrasures at Jiaoshan, Mt. Tu, Wulong Mountain, and elsewhere were reworked to meet specification.

sentences.zh: 五年，以外海兵輪統領駐吳淞口，凡沿海各省兵輪，悉歸調遣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the outer-sea steam commander was stationed at Wusong mouth; all steam warships of the coastal provinces were entirely subject to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 5 (1879), the outer-sea steam commander was posted at Wusong, with every coastal steamer under his orders.

sentences.zh: 七年，令彭玉麟籌辦江陰至吳淞口一帶海防。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Peng Yulin was ordered to organize coastal defense along the stretch from Jiangyin to Wusong mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 7 (1881), Peng Yulin was charged with Jiangyin-to-Wusong coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 重修圌山關、東生洲兩岸舊築砲堤，並築營壘，置大砲。

translations.literal: Old gun embankments on both banks at Mt. Tu pass and Dongsheng Isle were rebuilt, camps and ramparts also built, and large guns emplaced.
translations.idiomatic: Old gun embankments at Mt. Tu and Dongsheng Isle on both banks were rebuilt, barracks added, and heavy guns mounted.

sentences.zh: 又改天都廟舊式砲台為明砲台。

translations.literal: The old-style fort at Tiandu Temple was also converted into an open fort.
translations.idiomatic: Tiandu Temple's old battery was converted to an open fort.

sentences.zh: 八年，左宗棠舉辦沿海漁團，選漁戶精壯者五千人隸吳淞鎮，給以糧械，隨時操練。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Zuo Zongtang organized coastal fishing militia, selecting five thousand sturdy fishermen assigned to Wusong garrison, supplied with grain and arms, drilled at all times.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8 (1882), Zuo Zongtang raised a coastal fishing militia: five thousand stout fishermen enrolled under Wusong, provisioned and armed, and kept under drill.

sentences.zh: 彭玉麟以狼、福山為長江總口，長江下游雖修治砲台，而江面空虛，鐵甲大戰艦無多，止有海防，未能海戰。

translations.literal: Peng Yulin regarded Lang and Fushan as the Yangtze's main opening; though forts were repaired downstream, the river surface was empty, armored men-of-war were few—there was only coastal defense, unable to fight at sea.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yulin saw Lang and Fushan as the Yangtze's main gate. Downstream forts had been rebuilt, but the river was thinly held and armored capital ships scarce—coastal defense there was, not a fleet that could meet the enemy at sea.

sentences.zh: 議造鐵甲小兵艦十艘，專顧內洋，與砲台相掩護。

translations.literal: It was proposed to build ten small armored warships, devoted solely to the inner seas, mutually shielding with the forts.
translations.idiomatic: Ten small armored gunboats were proposed for inland waters, acting in concert with the forts.

sentences.zh: 十年，令安徽疆臣籌備上游江防。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Anhui's frontier officials were ordered to prepare upper-reach river defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 (1884), Anhui's governors were told to ready the upper Yangtze defenses.

sentences.zh: 乃於安慶城外，築明暗砲台各一座，石營一座。

translations.literal: Thereupon outside Anqing city one open and one concealed fort were each built, and one stone barracks.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Anqing they built one open and one masked battery and a stone barracks.

sentences.zh: 攔江磯北岸，建明砲台二座，石營一座，南岸建明砲台、石營各一座。

translations.literal: On the north bank of Lanjiang Ji, two open forts and one stone barracks were built; on the south bank one open fort and one stone barracks were each built.
translations.idiomatic: At Lanjiang Ji the north bank received two open batteries and a stone barracks; the south bank one open battery and one stone barracks.

sentences.zh: 西梁山建明砲台四座，石營一座，土營二座。

translations.literal: At West Liang Mountain four open forts, one stone barracks, and two earthen barracks were built.
translations.idiomatic: West Liang Mountain gained four open batteries, a stone barracks, and two earthen camps.

sentences.zh: 東梁山就其形勢，築石城、砲堤各一道，以控制江面。

translations.literal: At East Liang Mountain, following its terrain, one stone wall and one gun embankment were built to control the river surface.
translations.idiomatic: East Liang Mountain, following its contours, got a stone wall and gun embankment to command the river.

sentences.zh: 十年，曾國荃以新購西洋十四口徑八百磅子大砲及開花子彈，分置江陰、吳淞二口砲台。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Zeng Guoquan with newly purchased Western fourteen-inch guns firing eight-hundred-pound shells and explosive shells distributed them to the forts at Jiangyin and Wusong openings.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 (1884), Zeng Guoquan placed newly purchased 14-inch guns firing 800-pound shells and explosive rounds at the Jiangyin and Wusong batteries.

sentences.zh: 又購馬梯尼快槍二千枝，分給各營。

translations.literal: Two thousand Martini rapid-fire rifles were also purchased and distributed to each battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand Martini rifles were bought as well and issued to the battalions.

sentences.zh: 又於吳淞砲台增兵八營，江陰砲台增兵十二營，扼守江海總路。

translations.literal: At Wusong Fort eight more battalions were added; at Jiangyin Fort twelve more battalions were added, to choke off the main route of river and sea.
translations.idiomatic: Eight battalions were added at Wusong and twelve at Jiangyin to hold the main junction of river and sea traffic.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又增建吳淞、江陰砲台，以鐵木石土各料築成，各設新式後膛大砲，其旁佐以哈乞開司砲。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Wusong and Jiangyin forts were further expanded and built, constructed from iron, wood, stone, and earth materials; each was fitted with new-style breech-loading heavy guns, supplemented on the flanks with Hotchkiss guns.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 13 (1887), Wusong and Jiangyin batteries were rebuilt in iron, timber, stone, and earth, each mounting new breech-loading guns with Hotchkiss pieces in support.

sentences.zh: 江陰之四門大砲台，分建於小角山、黃山二處。
