translations.literal: Jiangyin's four-gate heavy gun fort was separately built at two places: Xiaojiao Mountain and Huangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin's four-embrasure heavy battery was split between Xiaojiao Mountain and Huangshan.

sentences.zh: 黃山舊砲台所存之八十磅子後膛砲，移設於大石灣明砲台。

translations.literal: The eighty-pound-shell breech-loading guns stored at the old Huangshan fort were moved and emplaced at the Dashiwan open fort.
translations.idiomatic: The 80-pound breech-loaders held at the old Huangshan battery were shifted to the open fort at Dashiwan.

sentences.zh: 凡砲台之門，各建砲房，護以三合土牆。

translations.literal: At every fort gate, gun rooms were each built, protected by concrete walls.
translations.idiomatic: Each fort entrance got a gun chamber shielded by concrete walls.

sentences.zh: 又田雞砲為軍中利器，於江干要隘，建砲房，置田雞砲，以資操練。

translations.literal: Frog guns were also sharp weapons in the army; at key passes along the riverbank, gun rooms were built and frog guns emplaced for drill practice.
translations.idiomatic: Frog mortars, prized infantry weapons, were housed in riverside gun rooms at critical points for training.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，張之洞以江南各砲台分為四路，南路獅子林、南石塘各台為一路，南北岸各台為一路，象山、焦山、圌山關、天都廟各台為一路，江寧之獅子山、幕府山、鍾山、下關各台為一路，設總管砲台官四員，以新購外洋四十餘磅子快槍砲三十具分置各砲台。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Zhang Zhidong divided Jiangnan's forts into four routes: the southern-route Lion Grove Forest and South Shitang forts as one route; north and south bank forts as one route; Xiangshan, Jiaoshan, Mt. Tu pass, and Tiandu Temple forts as one route; Jiangning's Lion Mountain, Mufu Mountain, Zhong Mountain, and Xiaguan forts as one route; four general superintendents of forts were established, and thirty newly purchased foreign quick-firing guns of more than forty pounds each were distributed among the forts.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 22 (1896), Zhang Zhidong reorganized Jiangnan's batteries into four sectors—Lion Grove and South Shitang on the south; all north- and south-bank posts; Xiangshan, Jiaoshan, Mt. Tu, and Tiandu Temple; and Jiangning's Lion Hill, Mufu Hill, Bell Hill, and Xiaguan—appointing four fort superintendents and distributing thirty newly bought foreign quick-firers of 40-plus pounds among them.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以長江水師兵力單弱，皖省防軍尤少，令沿江督撫，不分畛域，節節設防。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, because the Yangtze naval forces were few and weak and Anhui's defense troops were especially scant, the river-bank governors-general and governors were ordered, without regard to jurisdictional boundaries, to set defenses at every segment.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 25 (1899), with the Yangtze flotilla too thin and Anhui's garrison especially sparse, riverside governors were told to ignore provincial lines and fortify every stretch.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，以東南各省新軍，次第練成，命兵部侍郎鐵良至江南考察江海防務。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, because the new armies of the southeastern provinces were trained successively to completion, Vice Minister of War Tie Liang was ordered to Jiangnan to inspect river and sea defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 31 (1905), with southeastern new armies coming up to strength in turn, Vice Minister of War Tie Liang was sent to Jiangnan to review river and sea defenses.

sentences.zh: 旋鐵良覆陳江南之沿江海砲台，分為四路，曰吳淞，曰江陰，曰鎮江，曰金陵。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Tie Liang memorialized again that Jiangnan's river- and sea-facing forts were divided into four routes, called Wusong, Jiangyin, Zhenjiang, and Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Liang soon reported back that Jiangnan's river and coastal batteries fell into four sectors: Wusong, Jiangyin, Zhenjiang, and Jinling.

sentences.zh: 第一路吳淞砲台，在寶山縣南，分設三台，置前後膛大小砲三十四具，砲勇三百餘人，水旱雷營二哨，雷勇一百餘人，以盛字五營駐防。

translations.literal: The first route, Wusong Fort, lay south of Baoshan County; three forts were separately set up, with thirty-four muzzle- and breech-loading guns large and small emplaced, more than three hundred gunners, two platoons of naval and land mine companies, more than one hundred mine operators, garrisoned by five Sheng-character battalions.
translations.idiomatic: First sector: Wusong, south of Baoshan County—three batteries mounting thirty-four guns of mixed calibers, 300-plus gunners, two naval and land mine platoons with 100-plus sappers, garrisoned by five Sheng battalions.

sentences.zh: 第二路江陰砲台，在縣城北，於長江南北岸分設砲台，南岸置前後膛大小砲三十七具，北岸置砲二十具，砲勇共四百餘人，水旱雷營三哨，雷勇二百餘人，以合字、南字等八營分兩岸駐守。

translations.literal: The second route, Jiangyin Fort, lay north of the county seat; forts were separately set on both north and south banks of the Yangtze; on the south bank thirty-seven muzzle- and breech-loading guns large and small were emplaced, on the north bank twenty guns; gunners totaled more than four hundred; three platoons of naval and land mine companies, more than two hundred mine operators; eight battalions such as He-character and Nan-character battalions garrisoned the two banks separately.
translations.idiomatic: Second sector: Jiangyin, north of the county seat—batteries on both Yangtze banks with thirty-seven guns south and twenty north, 400-plus gunners, three mine platoons with 200-plus sappers, held by eight battalions including He and Nan units split between the shores.

sentences.zh: 第三路鎮江砲台五處，曰圌山關，曰東生洲，曰象山，曰焦山，曰天都廟。

translations.literal: The third route had five Zhenjiang forts, called Mt. Tu pass, Dongsheng Isle, Xiangshan, Jiaoshan, and Tiandu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Third sector: five Zhenjiang batteries—Mt. Tu, Dongsheng Isle, Xiangshan, Jiaoshan, and Tiandu Temple.

sentences.zh: 南岸各台置砲十五具，北岸各台置砲六具，砲勇二百餘人，以新湘二旗駐防。

translations.literal: Each south-bank fort emplaced fifteen guns, each north-bank fort six guns; more than two hundred gunners; garrisoned by the New Xiang two banners.
translations.idiomatic: South-bank posts held fifteen guns each, north-bank six; 200-plus gunners manned them under the New Xiang two banners.

sentences.zh: 溯江至鎮江府城，南岸象山，北岸天都廟，中流焦山，分設三台，象山置砲十八具，焦山六具，天都廟九具，砲勇三百餘人，以武威六營、新湘三旗駐防。

translations.literal: Upstream to Zhenjiang prefectural city, on the south bank Xiangshan, on the north bank Tiandu Temple, midstream Jiaoshan—three forts separately set; Xiangshan emplaced eighteen guns, Jiaoshan six, Tiandu Temple nine; more than three hundred gunners; garrisoned by six Wuwei battalions and three New Xiang banners.
translations.idiomatic: Upriver from Zhenjiang city—Xiangshan on the south bank, Tiandu Temple on the north, Jiaoshan midstream—three batteries with eighteen, six, and nine guns respectively, 300-plus gunners, garrisoned by six Wuwei battalions and three New Xiang banners.

sentences.zh: 金陵城外砲台七處，曰烏龍山，曰幕府山，曰下關，曰獅子山，曰富貴山，曰清涼山，曰雨花台。

translations.literal: Outside Jinling city were seven forts, called Wulong Mountain, Mufu Mountain, Xiaguan, Lion Mountain, Fugui Mountain, Qingliang Mountain, and Yuhuatai.
translations.idiomatic: Seven batteries ringed Jinling—Wulong Hill, Mufu Hill, Xiaguan, Lion Hill, Fugui Hill, Qingliang Hill, and Yuhuatai.

sentences.zh: 烏龍山在省城外四十里，於南岸分設五台，置砲十二具，砲勇一百餘人。

translations.literal: Wulong Mountain was forty li outside the provincial city; on the south bank five forts were separately set, with twelve guns emplaced, more than one hundred gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Wulong Hill, forty li outside the provincial capital, had five south-bank batteries with twelve guns and 100-plus gunners.

sentences.zh: 幕府山在北門外，砲台依次置砲七具，迤西老虎山置砲四具，砲勇一百餘人。

translations.literal: Mufu Mountain was outside the north gate; the fort successively emplaced seven guns; proceeding west, Laohu Mountain emplaced four guns; more than one hundred gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Mufu Hill, beyond the north gate, mounted seven guns; Laohu Hill farther west had four—100-plus gunners between them.

sentences.zh: 下關砲台在城外東面對岸，東岸置砲二具，西岸置砲十具，砲勇一百餘人。

translations.literal: Xiaguan Fort was on the opposite bank east of outside the city; the east bank emplaced two guns, the west bank ten guns; more than one hundred gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaguan battery faced the city's east bank—two guns on the east shore, ten on the west—manned by 100-plus gunners.

sentences.zh: 獅子山在城內，分設東西二台，置砲八具，砲勇九十人。

translations.literal: Lion Mountain was inside the city; east and west forts were separately set, with eight guns emplaced, ninety gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Lion Hill inside the city had east and west batteries with eight guns and ninety gunners.

sentences.zh: 富貴山在鍾山之麓，置砲六具，砲勇四十餘人。

translations.literal: Fugui Mountain was at the foot of Zhong Mountain; six guns were emplaced, more than forty gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Fugui Hill at the foot of Bell Hill mounted six guns with 40-plus gunners.

sentences.zh: 清涼山在西門內，依城為砲台，置砲二具，砲勇十四人。

translations.literal: Qingliang Mountain was inside the west gate; relying on the city wall as a fort, two guns were emplaced, fourteen gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Qingliang Hill inside the west gate used the city wall as its parapet—two guns, fourteen gunners.

sentences.zh: 雨花台在聚寶門外，置砲二具，砲勇十四人。

translations.literal: Yuhuatai was outside Jubao Gate; two guns were emplaced, fourteen gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhuatai, outside Jubao Gate, had two guns and fourteen gunners.

sentences.zh: 安徽省砲台分為四路，曰東西梁山，曰攔江磯，曰前江，曰棋盤山。

translations.literal: Anhui Province's forts were divided into four routes, called East and West Liang Mountains, Lanjiang Ji, Qianjiang, and Qipan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui's batteries fell into four sectors—East and West Liang Mountains, Lanjiang Ji, Qianjiang, and Qipan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 梁山夾江對峙，東台置砲十四具，西台十二具，以精銳營步兵三哨為砲兵。

translations.literal: Liang Mountains faced each other across the river; the east fort emplaced fourteen guns, the west twelve; three platoons of the Elite Battalion infantry served as gunners.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Mountains faced off across the river—fourteen guns east, twelve west—manned by three elite-infantry platoons converted to artillery.

sentences.zh: 攔江磯砲台在省城外四十里西岸，置砲十五具，以續備步隊中營駐台為砲兵。

translations.literal: Lanjiang Ji Fort was on the west bank forty li outside the provincial city; fifteen guns were emplaced; the Reserve Infantry Middle Battalion garrisoned the fort as gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Lanjiang Ji, forty li west of the provincial city, mounted fifteen guns under the reserve infantry middle battalion.

sentences.zh: 前江口砲台在上游十餘里，踞東岸高阜，分上下二台，置砲十二具，由續備中營撥兵分駐。

translations.literal: Qianjiang Mouth Fort was more than ten li upstream, occupying a high mound on the east bank; upper and lower forts were separately set, with twelve guns emplaced; troops were allocated from the Reserve Middle Battalion to garrison separately.
translations.idiomatic: Qianjiang Mouth, ten-plus li upstream on an east-bank height, split into upper and lower batteries with twelve guns, manned by detachments from the reserve middle battalion.

sentences.zh: 棋盤山砲台在安慶東門外北岸，置大小砲六十八具，以步兵前營駐防。

translations.literal: Qipan Mountain Fort was on the north bank outside Anqing's east gate; sixty-eight guns large and small were emplaced; garrisoned by the Infantry Front Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Qipan Mountain, on the north bank outside Anqing's east gate, held sixty-eight guns of assorted calibers under the infantry front battalion.

sentences.zh: 江西省砲台分為四路，曰馬當，曰湖口，曰金雞坡，曰岳師門。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Province's forts were divided into four routes, called Madang, Hukou, Jinji Slope, and Yueshi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi's batteries formed four sectors—Madang, Hukou, Jinji Slope, and Yueshi Gate.

sentences.zh: 馬當在彭澤縣東南岸，分設五台，置砲五具，砲勇六十人。

translations.literal: Madang was on Pengze County's southeast bank; five forts were separately set, with five guns emplaced, sixty gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Madang, on Pengze's southeast bank, had five batteries with five guns and sixty gunners.

sentences.zh: 湖口砲台在縣城北之東西岸，分設二台，置砲十具，砲勇七十人。

translations.literal: Hukou Fort was on the east and west banks north of the county seat; two forts were separately set, with ten guns emplaced, seventy gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Hukou, on both banks north of the county seat, had two batteries, ten guns, and seventy gunners.

sentences.zh: 金雞坡砲台在九江府十里外東西岸，分設三台，列東西北三面，置砲十二具，砲勇二百人。

translations.literal: Jinji Slope Fort was on the east and west banks ten li outside Jiujiang Prefecture; three forts were separately set, arrayed on east, north, and west faces, with twelve guns emplaced, two hundred gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Jinji Slope, ten li from Jiujiang on both banks, had three batteries facing east, north, and west with twelve guns and two hundred gunners.

sentences.zh: 岳師門砲台在九江東門外，分上下二台，沿江岸建築，置砲二十一具，砲勇七十人。

translations.literal: Yueshi Gate Fort was outside Jiujiang's east gate; upper and lower forts were separately set, built along the riverbank, with twenty-one guns emplaced, seventy gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Yueshi Gate, outside Jiujiang's east gate, had upper and lower shore batteries with twenty-one guns and seventy gunners.

sentences.zh: 湖北省砲台，僅田家鎮一路，分中南北三台，置砲三十一具，砲勇五十人。

translations.literal: Hubei Province's forts had only the Tianjiazhen route; middle, south, and north forts were separately set, with thirty-one guns emplaced, fifty gunners.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei had but one battery sector at Tianjiazhen—central, south, and north forts with thirty-one guns and fifty gunners.

sentences.zh: 自同治間，經營江海防務，歷四十餘年，始稱完密雲。

translations.literal: From the Tongzhi era, managing river and sea defenses, over more than forty years, it was only then called complete and tight.
translations.idiomatic: River and sea defenses had been under construction since the Tongzhi era; only after forty-odd years were they deemed complete.

sentences.zh: 浙江東南境瀕海者，為杭、嘉、寧、紹、溫、台六郡，凡一千三百餘里。

translations.literal: Zhejiang's southeastern border facing the sea comprised six prefectures—Hang, Jia, Ning, Shao, Wen, and Tai—totaling more than 1,300 li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang's coastal southeast comprised six prefectures—Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Ningbo, Shaoxing, Wenzhou, and Taizhou—stretching over 1,300 li.

sentences.zh: 南連閩嶠，北接蘇、松。

translations.literal: To the south it connected with Fujian's peaks; to the north it joined Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian's coast lay to the south, Suzhou and Songjiang to the north.

sentences.zh: 自平湖、海鹽西南至錢塘江口，折而東南至定海、舟山，為內海之堂奧。

translations.literal: From Pinghu and Haiyan southwest to Qiantang River mouth, turning southeast to Dinghai and Zhoushan, was the inner sea's vital core.
translations.idiomatic: From Pinghu and Haiyan southwest to the Qiantang estuary, then southeast to Dinghai and Zhoushan, lay the inner sea's heartland.

sentences.zh: 自鎮海而南，歷寧波、溫、台三府，直接閩境，東俯滄溟，皆外海。

translations.literal: From Zhenhai southward, passing Ningbo and Wen and Tai three prefectures, directly reaching Fujian's border, overlooking the vast eastern sea—all outer sea.
translations.idiomatic: South from Zhenhai through Ningbo, Wenzhou, and Taizhou to the Fujian border, all waters opening onto the open Pacific—outer sea throughout.

sentences.zh: 論防內海，則嘉興之乍浦、澉浦，海寧之洋山，杭州之鱉子門，紹興之沙門為要。

translations.literal: Speaking of defending the inner sea, then Jiaxing's Zha Pu and Gan Pu, Haining's Yangshan, Hangzhou's Biezi Gate, and Shaoxing's Shamen were key points.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-sea defense turned on Jiaxing's Zhapu and Ganpu, Haining's Yangshan, Hangzhou's Biezi Gate, and Shaoxing's Shamen.

sentences.zh: 論防外海，則定海縣與玉環廳皆孤峙大洋。

translations.literal: Speaking of defending the outer sea, then Dinghai County and Yuhuan Subprefecture both stood alone in the great ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Outer-sea defense hinged on Dinghai County and Yuhuan Subprefecture, each isolated in the open ocean.

sentences.zh: 定海為甬郡之屏籓，玉環為溫、台之保障，尤屬浙防重地。

translations.literal: Dinghai was Ningbo prefecture's screen and bulwark; Yuhuan was Wen and Tai's safeguard—especially key points of Zhejiang defense.
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai screened Ningbo; Yuhuan guarded Wenzhou and Taizhou—both linchpins of Zhejiang's coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 定海之東，其遠勢羅列者，首為海中之馬跡山。

translations.literal: East of Dinghai, among the distant formations arrayed in ranks, the foremost was Mazhi Mountain in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: East of Dinghai, the foremost of the distant islands was Mazhi Mountain at sea.

sentences.zh: 山北屬江蘇境，山南屬浙江境，而五奎山亦為扼要。

translations.literal: The mountain's north belonged to Jiangsu territory, its south to Zhejiang territory; and Wukui Mountain was also a choke point.
translations.idiomatic: Its north lay in Jiangsu, its south in Zhejiang; Wukui Mountain was another critical outpost.

sentences.zh: 陳錢山則在馬跡之東北，山大而隩廣，可為舟師屯泊之所。

translations.literal: Chenqian Mountain was northeast of Mazhi; the mountain was large and its bay wide, suitable as a place for the fleet to anchor and moor.
translations.idiomatic: Chenqian Hill northeast of Mazhi was large with a broad anchorage—a natural fleet mooring.

sentences.zh: 迤南經岱山、普陀山，出落迦門，至東霍山，與陳錢山南北相為犄角。

translations.literal: Proceeding south through Daishan and Putuo Mountain, exiting Luojia Gate, reaching Donghuo Mountain—it and Chenqian Mountain south and north served as pincer horns to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Southward through Daishan and Putuo, out Luojia Gate to Donghuo Hill, pairing with Chenqian in a north-south pincer.

sentences.zh: 其南有昌國外之韭山，均可駐泊舟師。

translations.literal: To its south was Jiushan outside Changguo—all suitable for mooring the fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south lay Jiushan beyond Changguo—another suitable fleet anchorage.

sentences.zh: 自寧波而南，內有佛頭、桃渚、松門、楚門諸山，外有茶盤、牛頭、積穀、石塘、大小鹿山，為溫、台所屬水師會哨之所。

translations.literal: From Ningbo southward, within were Fotou, Taozhu, Songmen, and Chumen mountains; without were Chapan, Niutou, Jigu, Shitang, and large and small Luzhi mountains—the places where Wen and Tai naval forces met for joint patrol.
translations.idiomatic: South of Ningbo, inner islands included Fotou, Taozhu, Songmen, and Chumen; outer ones Chapan, Niutou, Jigu, Shitang, and the Luzhi islets—joint patrol stations for Wenzhou and Taizhou flotillas.

sentences.zh: 由玉環廳而更南，歷漁山、三盤、鳳凰、北屺、南屺而至此關，則接閩省防地矣。

translations.literal: From Yuhuan Subprefecture proceeding further south, passing Yushan, Sanpan, Fenghuang, Beiqi, and Nanqi to reach this pass—then it joined Fujian Province's defense territory.
translations.idiomatic: South from Yuhuan through Yushan, Sanpan, Fenghuang, Beiqi, and Nanqi to this frontier lay Fujian's defense zone.

sentences.zh: 清初平定浙江後，沿明制嚴海防。

translations.literal: After the early Qing pacified Zhejiang, it followed the Ming system for strict coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: Once the early Qing had pacified Zhejiang, it tightened coastal defense along Ming lines.

sentences.zh: 順治八年，令寧波、溫州、台州三府沿海居民內徙，以絕海盜之蹤。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, the coastal residents of the three prefectures of Ningbo, Wenzhou, and Taizhou were ordered to move inland, in order to cut off the traces of pirates.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, coastal inhabitants of Ningbo, Wenzhou, and Taizhou were ordered to relocate inland, so that pirates might find no foothold along the shore.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，於沿海立椿界，增設墩堠台寨，駐兵警備。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, a pile boundary was established along the coast, additional beacon towers, watch posts, and fortified camps were set up, and troops were stationed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2, the coast was marked with a pile boundary, new beacon towers, watch posts, and fortified camps were added, and garrisons were posted to stand watch.

sentences.zh: 四年，以欽差大臣巡視浙江海防。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an imperial commissioner was appointed to inspect Zhejiang coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, an imperial commissioner was dispatched to inspect coastal defenses in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 七年，命偕總督出巡沿海，直至福建邊境，提督則每年必巡歷各海口，增造巨艦，備戰守。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was ordered to accompany the governor-general on a coastal inspection tour as far as the Fujian border; the provincial commander-in-chief, for his part, was required each year to tour every harbor mouth, and large warships were added in preparation for offense and defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was ordered to join the governor-general on a coastal tour all the way to the Fujian border, while the provincial commander-in-chief had to inspect every harbor mouth annually; more large warships were built for war and defense.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，命江、浙二省疆臣，會勘轄境海面，分界巡哨，勒石于洋山，垂為定制。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the frontier officials of the two provinces of Jiangsu and Zhejiang were ordered jointly to survey the sea surface within their jurisdictions, establish boundaries for patrol, and erect a stele on Yangshan, fixing this as a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, officials of Jiangsu and Zhejiang were ordered to survey the seas under their jurisdictions together, divide patrol zones, and set up a boundary marker on Yangshan—a rule thereafter treated as permanent.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，以提標之游擊、守備二員，統率兵丁，改隸水師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, the two officers—a brigade commander and a garrison commander—under the provincial commander's banner, who commanded the soldiers, were transferred to the naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5, the brigade commander and garrison commander under the provincial commander's banner, together with the troops they led, were transferred to the naval service.

sentences.zh: 六年，定沿海商船漁船之帆檣符號，以別奸良，並增設汛弁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, sail and mast markings for coastal merchant and fishing vessels were fixed in order to distinguish the wicked from the good, and additional garrison officers were also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, standardized sail and mast markings were imposed on coastal merchant and fishing craft to tell loyal traffic from smugglers and pirates, and more garrison officers were posted.

sentences.zh: 選福建之精練水兵至浙，教練浙軍十二營水戰諸務，巡遊海口。

translations.literal: Elite naval troops were selected from Fujian and sent to Zhejiang to train the twelve Zhejiang battalions in all matters of naval warfare, and to patrol the harbor mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Seasoned sailors were brought from Fujian to drill Zhejiang's twelve battalions in naval tactics and to patrol the coastal harbors.

sentences.zh: 七年，增建沿海要口台，增設巡船，及防汛移駐之區，總兵官出巡之制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, forts were added at key coastal points, patrol vessels were increased, zones for seasonal garrison relocations were fixed, and a system was established for regional commanders' inspection tours.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, coastal strongpoints were fortified, patrol ships were added, zones for seasonal redeployment of garrison troops were fixed, and a schedule was set for regional commanders' inspection tours.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十九年，以五奎山為浙洋扼要之地，撥定海標兵駐守。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong, Wukui Mountain was regarded as a strategic choke point on the Zhejiang sea routes, and troops from the Dinghai banner were assigned to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 59, Wukui Mountain was judged a vital point on the Zhejiang coast, and Dinghai garrison troops were posted there.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年，奇明保等以杭州之鱉子門，為錢塘通海要口，於潮神廟江狹之處，屯兵防守。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Daoguang, Qi Mingbao and others, holding that Biezi Gate at Hangzhou was the key opening through which the Qiantang River reached the sea, stationed troops to defend the narrow stretch of river by the Tide God Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 20, Qi Mingbao and his colleagues argued that Biezi Gate near Hangzhou was the Qiantang River's main outlet to the sea, and posted troops at the river narrows by the Tide God Temple.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，令沿海疆臣，仿定海土堡之法，凡近海村落，招募團練，築土堡，互相聯絡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, coastal frontier officials were ordered, following the method of the Dinghai earthen forts, to recruit militia in every village near the sea, build earthen forts, and link them with one another.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, coastal officials were told to follow Dinghai's model of earthen forts: recruit militia in seaside villages, build earthworks, and connect them into a network.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以漁山孤懸海外，令黃岩鎮總兵以舟師靖盜。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, because Yushan stood isolated far out at sea, the regional commander at Huangyan Town was ordered to pacify bandits there with a fleet.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, because Yushan lay exposed and alone far offshore, the Huangyan garrison commander was ordered to send ships against the pirates there.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，譚鍾麟以浙省沿海各口，巨艦之可深入者，距省最近為乍浦，次則寧波之鎮海、定海、石浦，台州之海門，溫州之黃華關，舊有砲台三十餘座，惟海門鎮砲台建築合法。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu, Tan Zhonglin reported that among the coastal openings of Zhejiang where large warships could penetrate deeply, Zhapu was nearest the provincial capital, followed by Zhenhai, Dinghai, and Shipu in Ningbo; Haimen in Taizhou; and Huanghua Pass in Wenzhou; more than thirty forts had existed, but only the fort at Haimen Town was properly built.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6, Tan Zhonglin observed that of Zhejiang's coastal entrances where heavy ships could sail deep inland, Zhapu lay closest to the provincial capital, followed by Zhenhai, Dinghai, and Shipu in the Ningbo area, Haimen in Taizhou, and Huanghua Pass in Wenzhou. More than thirty forts already stood along the coast, but only the one at Haimen Town was soundly built.

sentences.zh: 其澉浦之長山，乍浦之陳山，定海之舟山，海門鎮之小港口各砲台，咸加修改。

translations.literal: The forts at Changshan in Ganpu, Chenshan in Zhapu, Zhoushan in Dinghai, and the small harbor at Haimen Town were all renovated.
translations.idiomatic: Forts at Changshan near Ganpu, Chenshan near Zhapu, Zhoushan in Dinghai, and the small harbor at Haimen Town were all rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 鎮海之金雞、招寶二山，於原有砲台外，增築金雞山嘴砲台一座。

translations.literal: At Jinji and Zhaobao, the two hills of Zhenhai, in addition to the existing forts, one new fort was built at the tip of Jinji Hill.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenhai's twin hills, Jinji and Zhaobao, a new battery was added on the promontory of Jinji Hill, beyond the forts already there.

sentences.zh: 十三年，劉秉璋以浙江海防，首重舟山，次以招寶、金雞二山為要塞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Liu Bingzhang held that in Zhejiang coastal defense, Zhoushan ranked first in importance, and next came the two strongpoints of Zhaobao and Jinji hills.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Liu Bingzhang argued that Zhejiang's coastal defense should center first on Zhoushan, and next on the twin fortresses of Zhaobao and Jinji hills.

sentences.zh: 乃酌度形勢，分建宏遠、平遠、綏遠、安遠砲台四座，置克魯伯後膛大小銅砲，東御蛟門海口。

translations.literal: He then weighed the terrain and separately built four forts—Hongyuan, Pingyuan, Suiyuan, and Anyuan—equipping them with Krupp breech-loading copper cannon large and small, to guard the Jiaomen harbor mouth to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the terrain, he built four batteries—Hongyuan, Pingyuan, Suiyuan, and Anyuan—armed with Krupp breech-loading brass guns of various calibers to guard Jiaomen harbor to the east.

sentences.zh: 十四年，砲榮光以浙江原有之營勇砲兵，已陸續汰弱留強，加以整練，鎮海新築砲台，及改造舊式砲台，皆已竣工，增置新購後膛巨砲，以新練之軍駐守。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Pao Rongguang reported that the camp soldiers and gunners originally in Zhejiang had one after another been weeded of the weak and kept the strong, then thoroughly drilled; the newly built forts at Zhenhai and the renovated old-style forts had all been completed; newly purchased breech-loading great guns were added, and newly trained troops were stationed to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Pao Rongguang reported that Zhejiang's garrison gunners had been thinned to keep only the best and put through rigorous training; Zhenhai's new batteries and renovated older ones were all finished; freshly bought breech-loading heavy guns were installed; and newly drilled troops were posted to man them.

sentences.zh: 十九年，譚鍾麟以浙江水師船僅五十餘艘，增紅單船八艘，助巡洋面。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Tan Zhonglin, noting that the Zhejiang naval fleet had only a little more than fifty vessels, added eight red-banded ships to help expand the patrol area.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, finding Zhejiang's naval force numbered barely fifty ships, Tan Zhonglin added eight red-banded junks to broaden patrol coverage.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，劉樹棠以浙江武備新軍左營操法最精，其陸軍水師前敵駐防洋槍隊各營，步伐分合進退，亦均嫻熟，飭分駐寧、台、三門灣各隘，並澉浦、乍浦沿海口岸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Liu Shutang, holding that the drill of the left battalion of Zhejiang's New Army for Military Preparedness was the most refined, and that the various battalions of foreign-rifle companies stationed on the front lines of the army and navy likewise all handled advancing, withdrawing, separating, and reuniting in step with practiced skill, ordered them posted separately at the passes of Ningbo, Taizhou, and Sanmen Bay, as well as the coastal openings of Ganpu and Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, Liu Shutang praised the left battalion of Zhejiang's New Army for Military Preparedness as the best drilled in the province, and noted that the foreign-rifle companies of the army and naval vanguard were equally expert in manoeuvres. He ordered them distributed to the passes at Ningbo, Taizhou, and Sanmen Bay, and to the coastal ports of Ganpu and Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，張曾敭建言，浙江象山港在定海之南，深入象山境六十六里，口寬而水深，群山環繞，作海軍根據地最宜。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, Zhang Zengyi submitted a memorial stating that Xiangshan Harbor in Zhejiang lay south of Dinghai, extending sixty-six li deep into Xiangshan territory; its mouth was wide and its waters deep, and mountains encircled it on all sides—making it ideally suited to serve as a naval base.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year, Zhang Zengyi proposed that Xiangshan Harbor south of Dinghai—sixty-six li deep into Xiangshan, with a wide mouth, deep water, and encircling mountains—was ideally suited to serve as a naval base.

sentences.zh: 尋諭南北洋大臣勘度經營。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, the ministers of the Northern and Southern Fleets were ordered to survey the site and carry out the project.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon ordered the ministers of the Northern and Southern Fleets to survey the site and develop it.

sentences.zh: 浙江海岸綿長，省垣據錢塘江上游，外恃龕、赭二山為口門，江狹沙橫，儼如天塹，敵艦卒難闌入。

translations.literal: Zhejiang's coast is long and unbroken; the provincial capital sits on the upper reaches of the Qiantang River, relying outward on the two hills of Kan and Zhe as its gate; the river is narrow and sandbars cross it—it is like a natural moat, and enemy warships can scarcely break through in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang's coastline stretches far. The provincial capital lies up the Qiantang River, guarded outward by the Kan and Zhe hills at its mouth; the river narrows and sandbars run across it like a natural moat, so enemy warships can hardly force their way in.

sentences.zh: 道光以後，海疆屢警，雖寧、台戒嚴，而不致牽動全局。

translations.literal: After the Daoguang reign, the maritime frontier was repeatedly alarmed; though Ningbo and Taizhou were placed on alert, the whole situation was not dragged into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: After Daoguang, the coast was repeatedly threatened, yet even when Ningbo and Taizhou went on alert, the province as a whole was not thrown into crisis.

sentences.zh: 中法之役，法艦曾至寧波洋面，招寶山砲台卻之。

translations.literal: During the Sino-French War, French warships once reached the waters off Ningbo, and Zhaobao Hill fort drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sino-French War, French ships approached Ningbo, only to be turned back by the battery on Zhaobao Hill.

sentences.zh: 此後遂無歐艦之蹤。

translations.literal: After this there were no further traces of European warships.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no European warships appeared again.

sentences.zh: 惟象山港天然形勝，與膠澳、旅順鼎峙而三，惜築港未成雲。

translations.literal: Only Xiangshan Harbor, by natural advantage of terrain, stood as one of three pillars with Jiaoao and Lüshun—but alas, harbor construction was never completed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshan Harbor's natural advantages rivaled those of Jiaoao and Lüshun—the three great sites—but the planned naval base was never finished.

sentences.zh: 福建東南沿海凡二千餘里，港澳凡三百六十餘處，要口凡二十餘處。

translations.literal: Fujian's southeastern coast totals more than two thousand li; bays and inlets total more than three hundred and sixty; key openings total more than twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian's southeastern coast runs more than two thousand li, with over three hundred bays and inlets and more than twenty strategic entrances.

sentences.zh: 額設水師二萬七千七百餘人，分三十一營，大小戰船二百六十六艘。

translations.literal: The naval force on the rolls numbered more than twenty-seven thousand seven hundred men, divided into thirty-one battalions, with two hundred sixty-six large and small warships.
translations.idiomatic: On paper the navy fielded more than 27,700 men in thirty-one battalions, with 266 warships large and small.

sentences.zh: 自清初以迄乾隆，削平鄭氏，三定台灣，及嘉慶間靖海之役，福建用兵海上，較他省為多。

translations.literal: From the early Qing through Qianlong, in suppressing the Zheng clan, thrice pacifying Taiwan, and in the campaign to pacify the seas during the Jiaqing reign, Fujian deployed forces at sea more than any other province.
translations.idiomatic: From the early Qing through Qianlong—crushing the Zheng regime, thrice pacifying Taiwan, and fighting pirates in the Jiaqing era—Fujian saw more naval warfare than any other province.

sentences.zh: 島嶼星羅，處處與台、澎相控制，故海防布置，尤為繁密。

translations.literal: Islands were scattered like stars, every point mutually restraining Taiwan and Penghu; therefore coastal defense dispositions were especially dense.
translations.idiomatic: Islands dotted the sea, each point balancing Taiwan and Penghu across the strait, so coastal defenses there were laid out with unusual density.

sentences.zh: 其州郡濱海者，為福寧、福州、興化、泉州、漳州五府，而台灣障其東方。

translations.literal: Its prefectures and districts facing the sea were the five prefectures of Funing, Fuzhou, Xinghua, Quanzhou, and Zhangzhou, with Taiwan shielding them to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Five coastal prefectures—Funing, Fuzhou, Xinghua, Quanzhou, and Zhangzhou—faced the sea, with Taiwan standing as a barrier to the east.

sentences.zh: 五府防務，各有注重之處。

translations.literal: Each of the five prefectures had its own points of emphasis in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the five prefectures had its own defensive priorities.

sentences.zh: 福寧重在各港口，自北境之南關山、沙埕港口迤邐而西南，為烏岐港口、鹽田港口、白馬門口、金垂港口、飛鸞江口、東沖總口，海舶之輕利者，隨處可入。

translations.literal: Funing placed its emphasis on the various harbor mouths: from Nanguan Hill and Shacheng Harbor in the northern border, winding southwest through Wuji Harbor, Yantian Harbor, Baima Pass, Jinchui Harbor, Feiluan River mouth, and Dongchong main pass—wherever swift, light merchant vessels could enter at will.
translations.idiomatic: Funing's defense focused on its harbors—from Nanguan Hill and Shacheng in the north, sweeping southwest through Wuji, Yantian, Baima Pass, Jinchui, Feiluan River, and Dongchong—any point where light, fast ships could slip in.

sentences.zh: 其外海島嶼較大者，為東西台、七星礁、浮瀛、大小崳山，足資屏衛。

translations.literal: The larger islands in the outer seas were East and West Platform, Qixing Reef, Fuying, and Greater and Lesser Yushan—all sufficient to serve as protective screens.
translations.idiomatic: Larger offshore islands—East and West Platform, Qixing Reef, Fuying, and Greater and Lesser Yushan—could serve as outlying shields.

sentences.zh: 此福寧之防也。

translations.literal: Such was the defense of Funing.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Funing's coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 福州重在閩江，以江口內為省治所在。

translations.literal: Fuzhou placed its emphasis on the Min River, taking the area within the river mouth as the seat of provincial administration.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou's defense centered on the Min River, whose inner reaches held the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 其外自北境松崎、江戶，經東西洛、南北竿塘、鼇江口，至閩江近口之琅崎島、金牌、五虎門，皆扼要之所。

translations.literal: Outward from the northern border at Songqi and Jianghu, passing East and West Luo, North and South Gantang, Aojiang mouth, to Langqi Island, Jinpai, and Wuhumen near the Min River's mouth—all were choke points.
translations.idiomatic: From Songqi and Jianghu in the north, through East and West Luo, North and South Gantang, and Aojiang mouth, down to Langqi Island, Jinpai, and Wuhumen near the Min River's entrance—each was a vital choke point.

sentences.zh: 入口經大小嶼、羅星塔，乃同、光間所創建之海軍船廠、軍械製造局，咸在於是。

translations.literal: Entering the mouth one passed Greater and Lesser Islets and Luoxing Pagoda—the naval shipyard and ordnance factory established during the Tongzhi and Guangxu reigns were both located there.
translations.idiomatic: Inward past Greater and Lesser Islets and Luoxing Pagoda lay the naval shipyard and ordnance factory built in the Tongzhi and Guangxu eras.

sentences.zh: 出口沿海而南，經梅花江口、龍江口，少東即海壇島，水師重鎮所在。

translations.literal: Exiting southward along the coast, passing Meihua River mouth and Longjiang mouth, a little to the east lay Haitan Island—the seat of a major naval garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Southward along the coast past Meihua and Longjiang river mouths, a short distance east lay Haitan Island, home to a major naval garrison.

sentences.zh: 其外海之島，若猴嶼受閩江之沖，東永當長樂之臂，較白大、東沙諸島為要。

translations.literal: Among the islands in the outer sea, Houyu bore the brunt of the Min River's flow, Dongyong guarded Changle's flank—they were more important than the islands of Baidai and Dongsha.
translations.idiomatic: Offshore, Houyu absorbed the Min River's force and Dongyong guarded Changle's flank—both more important than Baidai, Dongsha, and the other outlying islets.

sentences.zh: 此福州之防也。

translations.literal: Such was the defense of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Fuzhou's coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 興化重在海濱諸島，自三江口經鹿耳、大小丘，循平海衛、湄洲嶼，至雙溪港口，乃沿海之境。

translations.literal: Xinghua placed its emphasis on the islands along the seashore: from Sanjiang mouth through Deer Ear and Greater and Lesser Qiu, following Pinghaiwei and Meizhou Island to Shuangxi Harbor—these constituted the coastal zone.
translations.idiomatic: Xinghua's defense focused on its coastal islands—from Sanjiang mouth through Deer Ear and Greater and Lesser Qiu, along Pinghaiwei and Meizhou Island to Shuangxi Harbor.

sentences.zh: 其外海島嶼，為平海、南日二島，列汛置官，視為重地，而湄洲亦興郡屏籓。

translations.literal: Its outer-sea islands were the two islands of Pinghai and Nanri; garrisons and officials were posted there and the places were regarded as vital ground, while Meizhou also served as a protective screen for the Xinghua prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Its key offshore islands were Pinghai and Nanri, each garrisoned and treated as vital ground; Meizhou too served as Xinghua's outer shield.

sentences.zh: 此興化之防也。

translations.literal: Such was the defense of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Xinghua's coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 泉州重在金、廈二島。

translations.literal: Quanzhou placed its emphasis on the two islands of Kinmen and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhou's defense centered on the islands of Kinmen and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 自北境惠安峰、崎港口，經雒陽江、晉江、安海港三口。

translations.literal: From Huian Peak and Qi Harbor in the northern border, passing the three mouths of Luoyang River, Jin River, and Anhai Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: From Huian Peak and Qi Harbor in the north, through the mouths of the Luoyang, Jin, and Anhai rivers.

sentences.zh: 其南為金州鎮。

translations.literal: To its south was Jinzhou Town.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay Jinzhou garrison town.

sentences.zh: 又西經大登、小登，即廈門島。

translations.literal: Farther west, passing Daden and Xiaodeng, one reached Xiamen Island.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west, past Daden and Xiaodeng, lay Xiamen Island.

sentences.zh: 島北為同安港口。

translations.literal: North of the island was Tong'an Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: North of the island lay Tong'an Harbor.

sentences.zh: 金、廈二門，遠控台、澎，近衛泉、漳，為海防重地。

translations.literal: The two straits of Kinmen and Xiamen controlled Taiwan and Penghu from afar and guarded Quanzhou and Zhangzhou at close range—they were vital points of coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Kinmen and Xiamen straits commanded Taiwan and Penghu at a distance while shielding Quanzhou and Zhangzhou up close—making them among the most critical positions on the coast.

sentences.zh: 其外海之永寧、定安、烏潯諸島，亦設汛置兵。

translations.literal: On the outer-sea islands of Yongning, Ding'an, Wuxun, and others, garrisons were also established and troops stationed.
translations.idiomatic: Offshore islands such as Yongning, Ding'an, and Wuxun were likewise garrisoned and manned.

sentences.zh: 此泉州之防也。

translations.literal: Such was the defense of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Quanzhou's coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 漳州重在南澳，鼓浪嶼為南境盡處，尤擅形勢。

translations.literal: Zhangzhou placed its emphasis on Nan'ao; Gulangyu marked the southern extremity of its territory and was especially favored by terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou's defense focused on Nan'ao; Gulangyu, at the southern edge of its jurisdiction, commanded the finest strategic position.

sentences.zh: 其沿海之境，自九龍江口折而西南，經六鼇港、漳江二口，循銅山而南，為詔安港口。

translations.literal: Its coastal zone, from Jiulong River mouth turning southwest, passed the two mouths of Liu'ao Harbor and Zhang River, followed Tongshan southward, and reached Zhao'an Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Its coastal stretch ran from Jiulong River mouth southwest through Liu'ao Harbor and the Zhang River mouth, then south along Tongshan to Zhao'an Harbor.

sentences.zh: 其南隔海為南澳鎮，南疆要地，與粵海共之。

translations.literal: To its south, across the sea, was Nan'ao garrison town—a vital point of the southern frontier, shared with the Guangdong coast.
translations.idiomatic: Across the sea to the south lay Nan'ao garrison, a key southern stronghold shared with the Guangdong coast.

sentences.zh: 其外海島嶼，首為烏丘，最當衝要。

translations.literal: Among its outer-sea islands, Wuchiu came first—the most critical point of conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Offshore, Wuchiu Island stood foremost—the most exposed and contested position.

sentences.zh: 而鼓浪嶼當海門之口，與鎮海城砲台同為重地。

translations.literal: Gulangyu stood at the mouth of the sea gate, and together with the Zhenhai City battery was regarded as vital ground.
translations.idiomatic: Gulangyu guarded the sea gate, and together with the Zhenhai City battery it ranked among the most vital positions.

sentences.zh: 此漳州之防也。

translations.literal: Such was the defense of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Zhangzhou's coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 中國沿海各省，自浙洋而北，海濱淤沙多而島嶼少，其海岸徑直，故防務重在江海總口，而略于海岸。

translations.literal: Among China's coastal provinces, from the Zhejiang seas northward, the seashore had much silting and few islands; the coastline was straight. Therefore coastal defense emphasized the great mouths of rivers and seas, while the shoreline itself was given less attention.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Zhejiang seas, China's coastal provinces had muddy, silt-laden shores and few islands, with relatively straight coastlines—so coastal defense focused on major river and sea mouths rather than the shoreline itself.

sentences.zh: 自浙洋而南，島嶼多而淤沙少，其海岸紆曲，故防務既重海口，而巨島與海岸亦並重焉。

translations.literal: From the Zhejiang seas southward, islands were many and silting was less; the coastline was winding. Therefore coastal defense both emphasized harbor mouths, and large islands and the coast were equally weighted.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Zhejiang seas, islands were plentiful and silting less severe, with winding coastlines—so harbor mouths mattered, but large islands and the coast itself were equally vital.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年，王命岳以閩省之海門與廈門相望，左為鎮海衛，乃漳州府之門戶，同安縣之高浦城等處，地近廈門，為泉州府屏衛，乃屯兵於鎮海、高浦二城，而分營以防鄰近隘口。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi, Wang Mingyue observed that Fujian's sea gate faced Xiamen across the water; to the left was Zhenhaiwei—the gateway of Zhangzhou prefecture. At Gaopu City in Tong'an county and other places near Xiamen, the ground served as a protective screen for Quanzhou prefecture. Troops were garrisoned at the two cities of Zhenhai and Gaopu, and camps were divided to guard neighboring passes.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17, Wang Mingyue noted that Fujian's sea gate faced Xiamen across the strait. Zhenhaiwei to the left was Zhangzhou's gateway; Gaopu City in Tong'an county and other sites near Xiamen shielded Quanzhou. He garrisoned Zhenhai and Gaopu and deployed separate camps to guard the nearby passes.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，浙閩總督高其倬奏陳操練沿海水師，並令閩洋水師巡視本省各口，兼赴浙洋巡緝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, Zhejiang-Fujian Governor-General Gao Qizhuo memorialized urging drill of the coastal naval forces, and ordered the Fujian naval fleet to patrol the various mouths of the province, also going to the Zhejiang seas for patrol and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4, Governor-General Gao Qizhuo of Zhejiang and Fujian memorialized on drilling the coastal navy and ordered Fujian's fleet to patrol every port in the province while also conducting suppression patrols in Zhejiang waters.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，令閩省水師仿商船式改造戰船八十艘，編為兩列。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, the Fujian naval forces were ordered to refit eighty warships on the model of merchant vessels, organized into two columns.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4, Fujian's navy was ordered to refit eighty warships on merchant-ship designs, organized into two squadrons.

sentences.zh: 自泉州之崇武，分南北犄角。

translations.literal: From Chongwu in Quanzhou, they were divided into north and south pincers.
translations.idiomatic: From Chongwu in Quanzhou, the fleet split into northern and southern wings in pincer formation.

sentences.zh: 由崇武而南，令南澳、銅山、金門及提標後營各鎮將率船巡緝。

translations.literal: From Chongwu southward, the commanders of Nan'ao, Tongshan, Kinmen, and the Rear Camp of the Provincial Admiral were ordered to lead ships on patrol and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: South of Chongwu, the commanders of Nan'ao, Tongshan, Kinmen, and the provincial admiral's rear camp were ordered to lead patrol squadrons.

sentences.zh: 崇武而北，令海壇、閩安及金門右營各鎮將率船巡緝。

translations.literal: North of Chongwu, the commanders of Haitan, Min'an, and the Right Camp of Kinmen were ordered to lead ships on patrol and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: North of Chongwu, the commanders of Haitan, Min'an, and Kinmen's right camp were ordered to lead patrol squadrons.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年，諭鄧廷楨招募練勇，嚴守澎湖，以扼閩省赴台灣之路。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Daoguang, an edict instructed Deng Tingzhen to recruit and drill militia, strictly guard Penghu, and choke off the route from Fujian to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 20, Deng Tingzhen was ordered to recruit and drill militia, hold Penghu firmly, and block the route from Fujian to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，諭怡良等屯兵福州金牌各要口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, an edict instructed Yiliang and others to garrison troops at the vital mouths of Fuzhou's Jinpai.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, Yiliang and others were ordered to garrison troops at the key passes of Fuzhou's Jinpai.

sentences.zh: 其距省二十里外之洪塘河及少岐，均沈船布椿設防。

translations.literal: At Hongtang River and Shaoqi, twenty li beyond the provincial capital, sunken ships and planted stakes were deployed for defense.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongtang River and Shaoqi, twenty li from the provincial capital, defenses were set with sunken ships and driven stakes.

sentences.zh: 閩省門戶在外洋者，為五虎、芭蕉二口。

translations.literal: Among Fujian's gateways on the open sea were the two mouths of Wuhu and Bajiao.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian's outer gateways on the open sea were the Wuhu and Bajiao channels.

sentences.zh: 入口為壺江，水勢稍狹，無險可扼。

translations.literal: The entrance was Hujiang; the waters were somewhat narrow, with no strategic point that could be held.
translations.idiomatic: The entrance at Hujiang had relatively narrow waters, with no natural choke point to hold.

sentences.zh: 進至金牌、長門，有巨石橫亙中流，扼守較易。

translations.literal: Advancing to Jinpai and Changmen, great rocks stretched across midstream, making defense easier to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Farther in at Jinpai and Changmen, massive rocks spanned midstream, making the passage easier to defend.

sentences.zh: 又進乃閩安之南北岸，為水路總匯，兩山夾峙，可稱天險。

translations.literal: Still farther in were the north and south banks of Min'an—the confluence of waterways; two mountains flanked the channel, which could be called a heaven-sent barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Still farther lay Min'an's north and south banks, where all water routes converged between two facing mountains—a natural fortress.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，於南岸建鐵門暗砲台六、明砲台八，北岸建鐵門暗砲台七。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu, on the south bank six iron-gate concealed batteries and eight exposed batteries were built; on the north bank seven iron-gate concealed batteries.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6, six iron-gate concealed batteries and eight exposed batteries were built on the south bank, and seven iron-gate concealed batteries on the north.

sentences.zh: 七年，又於長門建暗砲台四、明砲台六，悉仿洋式。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, four concealed batteries and six exposed batteries were also built at Changmen, all modeled on Western designs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, four concealed and six exposed batteries were added at Changmen, all built to Western designs.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，增祺因閩省濱海，屯戍空虛，增練旗、綠各營，以厚兵力。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Zeng Qi, because Fujian bordered the sea and its garrisons were thin, increased drill among banner and Green Standard camps to strengthen military force.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24, Zeng Qi, finding Fujian's coastal garrisons undermanned, expanded drill across banner and Green Standard camps to thicken the province's defenses.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，許應騤以漳州之鼓浪嶼設防尚未周備，增建砲台，置新式砲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Xu Yingqi, because Gulangyu in Zhangzhou was not yet fully fortified, added batteries and installed new-style cannon.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 25, Xu Yingqi found Gulangyu's defenses incomplete and added batteries with modern artillery.

sentences.zh: 綜閩省海防，所注重者，隨時異宜。

translations.literal: Taking Fujian's coastal defense as a whole, what was emphasized varied with the needs of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Overall, Fujian's coastal defense priorities shifted with the demands of each era.

sentences.zh: 當康熙間，以鄭氏由台、澎據海壇、金、廈，故海防獨重泉、漳。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign, because the Zheng clan from Taiwan and Penghu held Haitan, Kinmen, and Xiamen, coastal defense singled out Quanzhou and Zhangzhou for special weight.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, with the Zheng regime holding Haitan, Kinmen, and Xiamen from bases in Taiwan and Penghu, coastal defense focused chiefly on Quanzhou and Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其時水師以沙唬船不適于海戰，改造鳥船。

translations.literal: At that time the naval forces found sand-junk ships unsuited to sea battle and converted to bird ships.
translations.idiomatic: The navy then found sand junks ill-suited to open-sea combat and converted to bird ships.

sentences.zh: 施琅之平台灣，即藉鳥船之力。

translations.literal: Shi Lang's pacification of Taiwan relied precisely on the power of bird ships.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lang's conquest of Taiwan owed much to the bird ships.

sentences.zh: 及嘉慶間，海盜蔡牽竄擾浙、閩、粵三省洋面，而閩省當其中，寧、福、興、泉、漳五郡皆剽掠經由之境，故列郡咸重海防。

translations.literal: By the Jiaqing reign, the pirate Cai Qian raided the seas of Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong; Fujian lay in the middle, and the five prefectures of Ning, Fu, Xing, Quan, and Zhang were all routes of his pillaging—thus every prefecture placed weight on coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: By Jiaqing, the pirate Cai Qian plagued the seas of Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong. Fujian lay at the center, and all five prefectures—Ning, Fu, Xing, Quan, and Zhang—lay in his path, so every district strengthened its coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 其時水師利用巨艦，李長庚造霆船三十艘，置大砲四百餘具，屢敗牽於閩海，卒合閩、浙水師之力，圍而殲之。

translations.literal: At that time the naval forces employed great warships; Li Changgeng built thirty thunder ships armed with more than four hundred great cannon, repeatedly defeating Cai Qian in Fujian waters, and finally combining the naval forces of Fujian and Zhejiang, surrounded and annihilated him.
translations.idiomatic: The navy then fielded heavy warships; Li Changgeng built thirty thunder ships mounting over four hundred large guns, repeatedly routed Cai Qian in Fujian waters, and finally, joining Fujian and Zhejiang fleets, surrounded and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 最後為光緒中法之戰，法人以大隊鐵艦專攻福州，故海防獨重閩江口，而各郡無驚。

translations.literal: Last came the Sino-French War of the Guangxu reign; the French with a fleet of ironclads focused their attack on Fuzhou, so coastal defense singled out the Min River mouth for special weight, while the other prefectures were undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Finally, in the Guangxu-era Sino-French War, French ironclads concentrated on Fuzhou, so coastal defense focused on the Min River mouth while the other prefectures went unscathed.

sentences.zh: 同治以後，創船廠，造鐵艦，築砲台，制槍砲，海防漸臻嚴密。

translations.literal: After the Tongzhi reign, shipyards were established, ironclads built, batteries constructed, and firearms and cannon manufactured—coastal defense gradually reached full rigor.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongzhi, shipyards, ironclads, batteries, and modern arms were built, and coastal defenses grew steadily more formidable.

sentences.zh: 乃馬江失律，盡隳前功，良足慨耳。

translations.literal: Yet the debacle at Mawei destroyed all prior achievements—a matter truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the disaster at Mawei undid all these gains—a loss truly to be mourned.

sentences.zh: 台灣西與福、興、泉、漳四府相值，距澎、廈各數百里。

translations.literal: Taiwan to the west faced the four prefectures of Fu, Xing, Quan, and Zhang; it was several hundred li from Penghu and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan faced Fujian's Fu, Xing, Quan, and Zhang prefectures to the west, several hundred li from Penghu and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 其山脈北起雞籠，南盡沙馬碕。

translations.literal: Its mountain ranges began in the north at Keelung and ended in the south at Samabachi.
translations.idiomatic: Its mountains ran from Keelung in the north to Samabachi in the south.

sentences.zh: 東西沃野，一歲三熟。

translations.literal: East and west were fertile plains yielding three harvests a year.
translations.idiomatic: Fertile plains east and west yielded three harvests a year.

sentences.zh: 宋稱毗舍那國。

translations.literal: In the Song it was called the state of Pizhena.
translations.idiomatic: The Song knew it as the land of Pizhena.

sentences.zh: 明季日本、荷蘭人迭踞之。

translations.literal: In the late Ming, Japanese and Dutch successively occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming, Japanese and Dutch alternately held it.

sentences.zh: 順治間，鄭成功佔台灣、金、廈，時犯泉、漳。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi, Zheng Chenggong held Taiwan, Kinmen, and Xiamen, and from time to time raided Quanzhou and Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi, Zheng Chenggong held Taiwan, Kinmen, and Xiamen and periodically raided Quanzhou and Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，姚啟聖以閩省水師三百艘討之，先克金、廈。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, Yao Qisheng with three hundred ships of the Fujian navy attacked him, first taking Kinmen and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi, Yao Qisheng led three hundred Fujian warships against him, first seizing Kinmen and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，施琅以水師二萬克台灣，乃置台灣府，設廳縣各官，鑄鐵幣，開學校，築城垣，逐生番，戍兵萬有四千，遂為海外重鎮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Shi Lang with twenty thousand naval troops conquered Taiwan. He then established Taiwan prefecture, appointed officials for departments and counties, cast iron coin, opened schools, built city walls, expelled the aborigines, and garrisoned fourteen thousand troops—it thus became a major stronghold overseas.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22, Shi Lang conquered Taiwan with twenty thousand sailors. He established Taiwan prefecture, appointed district and county officials, minted iron currency, opened schools, built fortifications, drove back the aborigines, and garrisoned fourteen thousand troops—making the island a major overseas stronghold.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年，硃一貴之叛，施世驃由廈門率水師六百艘進攻，七日而克之。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Kangxi, during the rebellion of Zhu Yigui, Shi Shipiao from Xiamen led six hundred naval ships in attack and took it in seven days.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 60, during Zhu Yigui's rebellion, Shi Shipiao led six hundred warships from Xiamen and captured the island in seven days.

sentences.zh: 乃以總兵官鎮台灣，副將守澎湖。

translations.literal: A regional commander was then stationed at Taiwan and a vice commander guarded Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: A regional commander was posted to Taiwan and a vice commander to Penghu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，福康安平林爽文之亂，台灣北境乃漸展拓。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign, Fuk'anggan pacified the rebellion of Lin Shuangwen, and Taiwan's northern border was gradually extended.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong, Fuk'anggan suppressed Lin Shuangwen's rebellion, and Taiwan's northern frontier was gradually expanded.

sentences.zh: 其山後之地，至嘉慶間始辟之。

translations.literal: The lands behind the mountains were not opened until the Jiaqing reign.
translations.idiomatic: The mountainous interior was not settled until the Jiaqing era.

sentences.zh: 光緒十三年，開台灣為省治，設巡撫以下各官，為中國海南右臂。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Guangxu, Taiwan was opened as a provincial seat; officials from the governor down were established, serving as the right arm of the sea south of China.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 13 (1887), Taiwan was elevated to full provincial status, with a governor and the complete provincial bureaucracy, forming China's strategic bulwark along the southern sea.

sentences.zh: 及中日之戰，割讓於日本，而疆事益不可問雲。

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese War came, it was ceded to Japan, and frontier affairs became even more impossible to inquire about.
translations.idiomatic: After the Sino-Japanese War, Taiwan was ceded to Japan, and the fate of the maritime frontier could no longer even be discussed.

sentences.zh: 廣東南境皆瀕海，自東而西，歷潮、惠、廣、肇、高、雷、廉七郡，而抵越南。

translations.literal: Guangdong's southern border all fronts the sea; from east to west it passes through the seven prefectures of Chao, Hui, Guang, Zhao, Gao, Lei, and Lian, reaching Vietnam.
translations.idiomatic: All of Guangdong's southern coast faces the sea. From east to west it runs through the seven prefectures of Chaozhou, Huizhou, Guangzhou, Zhaoqing, Gaozhou, Leizhou, and Lianzhou, reaching the border with Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 其東境始於南澳，與閩海接界。

translations.literal: Its eastern border begins at Nan'ao, meeting the boundary with Fujian's seas.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern frontier begins at Nan'ao, where it meets the Fujian coast.

sentences.zh: 潮郡支山入海，有廣澳、赤澳諸島，皆水師巡泊所在。

translations.literal: In Chaozhou prefecture, branches of mountains reach into the sea; there are Guang'ao, Chi'ao, and other islands—all places where the naval forces patrol and anchor.
translations.idiomatic: In Chaozhou, spurs of the mountains run out into the sea, where islands such as Guang'ao and Chi'ao lie—all of them anchorage points for naval patrols.

sentences.zh: 迤西為惠州，民性剽悍，與潮郡無異，設碣石鎮總兵以鎮之。

translations.literal: Continuing west is Huizhou; the people are fierce and bold, no different from Chaozhou, and a regional commander stationed at Jieshi garrison was appointed to keep order.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west lies Huizhou, whose people are as tough and unruly as those of Chaozhou; a regional commander was posted at Jieshi garrison to keep them in check.

sentences.zh: 又西為廣州境，其海灣深廣。

translations.literal: Farther west is Guangzhou territory; its bay is deep and broad.
translations.idiomatic: Still farther west is Guangzhou, whose harbor is deep and wide.

sentences.zh: 自新安折而北，又折而南，至香山，是為內海，群島環羅，為廣州省治之外護。

translations.literal: From Xin'an it turns north, then turns south again, reaching Xiangshan—this is the inner sea, with islands encircling all around, serving as the outer protection of Guangzhou's provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: From Xin'an the coast curves north, then south again to Xiangshan, forming the inner sea—a ring of islands that shielded the provincial capital of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又西為金州、馬鞍諸山，則肇郡陽江之屏障也。

translations.literal: Farther west are Mount Jinzhou, Mount Ma'an, and other peaks—they are the barrier screen for Yangjiang in Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west rise Mount Jinzhou, Mount Ma'an, and other peaks—the natural rampart behind Yangjiang in Zhaoqing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又西為高州海，多暗礁暗沙，海防較簡。

translations.literal: Farther west is the Gaozhou sea, with many hidden reefs and sandbars; coastal defense there was comparatively simpler.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west lies the Gaozhou coast, riddled with submerged reefs and sandbars; coastal defenses there were kept relatively light.

sentences.zh: 又西為雷州，其南幹突出三百餘里，三面皆海。

translations.literal: Farther west is Leizhou; its southern peninsula projects more than three hundred li, with sea on three sides.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west is Leizhou, whose southern peninsula juts out more than three hundred li, surrounded by sea on three sides.

sentences.zh: 渡海而南為瓊州。

translations.literal: Crossing the sea southward is Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: South across the sea lies Qiongzhou (Hainan).

sentences.zh: 又西為廉、欽，與越南錯壤。

translations.literal: Farther west are Lian and Qin, with territory interlocking with Vietnam.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west are Lianzhou and Qinzhou, on territory interleaved with Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 廉州多沙，欽州多島，襟山帶海，界接華夷。

translations.literal: Lian has much sand, Qin has many islands; girded by mountains and belted by sea, the border joins Chinese and barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: Lianzhou is mostly sandy flats, Qinzhou mostly islands; mountains behind and sea before, the frontier stood where China met foreign lands.

sentences.zh: 瓊州孤懸海表，其州縣環繞黎疆，沿海多沈沙，行舟至險，水師可寄泊港口僅有六七處。

translations.literal: Qiongzhou stands alone beyond the sea; its prefectures and counties surround Li territory. Along the coast there is much submerged sand; navigation is extremely perilous; ports where the naval forces could anchor numbered only six or seven.
translations.idiomatic: Qiongzhou lay isolated beyond the sea, its counties encircling Li territory. Submerged sandbanks made the coast treacherous to navigate, and the navy could find safe anchorage at only six or seven harbors.

sentences.zh: 此全境海防之形勢也。

translations.literal: This is the configuration of coastal defense for the entire region.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the overall coastal defense posture of the entire province.

sentences.zh: 廣州海防，自零丁洋過龍穴而北，兩山斜峙，東曰沙角，西曰大角，由此入內洋，為第一重隘。

translations.literal: Guangzhou's coastal defense: from Lintingyang, passing Longxue northward, two mountains stand obliquely facing each other—east is Shajiao, west is Dajiao. Entering the inner sea from here is the first barrier pass.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou's coastal defenses began at Lintingyang; passing Longxue to the north, two headlands faced each other across the channel—Shajiao to the east and Dajiao to the west. This gateway into the inner sea was the first line of defense.

sentences.zh: 進口七里有山曰橫當，前有小山曰下橫當，左為武山，亦曰南山，為海船所必經，乃第二重隘。

translations.literal: Seven li inside the entrance is a mountain called Hengdang; before it is a small mountain called Xiahengdang; to the left is Wushan, also called Nanshan—all routes sea vessels must take. This is the second barrier pass.
translations.idiomatic: Seven li inside the entrance stood Mount Hengdang, with the smaller Mount Xiahengdang before it and Wushan—also called Nanshan—on the left. Every ship had to pass through here—the second line of defense.

sentences.zh: 再進五里曰大虎山，西曰小虎山，又西曰獅子洋，乃黃埔入省城之路，為第三重隘。

translations.literal: Five li farther in is Dahu Mountain; west is Xiaohu Mountain; still west is Shizi Yang—it is the route from Huangpu into the provincial capital, the third barrier pass.
translations.idiomatic: Five li farther on lay Dahu Mountain, with Xiaohu Mountain to the west and still farther west Shizi Channel—the waterway from Huangpu to the provincial capital, the third line of defense.

sentences.zh: 歷朝於此雖築壘駐兵，而設備未周。

translations.literal: Though successive dynasties built fortifications and stationed troops here, the preparations were not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasties past had built fortifications and garrisoned troops here, but the defenses were never fully adequate.

sentences.zh: 歐艦東來，粵東首當其衝。

translations.literal: When European warships came east, eastern Guangdong bore the brunt first.
translations.idiomatic: When European fleets came east, eastern Guangdong was the first to take the blow.

sentences.zh: 道光禁煙之役，英艦進薄廣州內海，林則徐督粵，屢戰卻之。

translations.literal: During the Daoguang anti-opium campaign, British warships pressed close to Guangzhou's inner sea; Lin Zexu oversaw Guangdong and repeatedly fought them off.
translations.idiomatic: During the opium prohibition campaign under Daoguang, British ships pushed into Guangzhou's inner harbor; Lin Zexu, as governor-general of Guangdong, fought them back again and again.

sentences.zh: 其時布防較密，而壁塢皆循舊式。

translations.literal: At that time defenses were deployed more densely, but the ramparts and fortifications all followed old patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Defenses were then more tightly deployed, but the forts and batteries still followed outdated designs.

sentences.zh: 至光緒間，彭玉麟、張之洞守粵，始有曲折掩護之砲台，後膛連珠之槍砲，防務益嚴矣。

translations.literal: By the Guangxu era, when Peng Yulin and Zhang Zhidong guarded Guangdong, there were finally batteries with curving cover, breech-loading rapid-fire guns and cannon, and coastal defense grew stricter still.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the Guangxu era, under Peng Yulin and Zhang Zhidong, did Guangdong acquire batteries with angled cover and breech-loading repeating cannon—and coastal defenses grew truly formidable.

sentences.zh: 清初規制，設大小兵船一百數十艘，僅能巡防內洋，不能越境追捕，遇有寇盜，則賃用民船。

translations.literal: Under early Qing regulations, more than a hundred large and small warships were established; they could only patrol the inner sea and could not pursue across borders; when bandits appeared, civilian vessels were hired.
translations.idiomatic: Under early Qing regulations, a fleet of some 150 warships of various sizes could patrol only the inner sea, not chase raiders beyond provincial waters; when pirates struck, the navy had to hire merchant vessels to pursue them.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十六年，始建廣州海濱橫當、南山二處砲台。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year of Kangxi, batteries were first built at Hengdang and Nanshan on Guangzhou's seashore.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 56 (1717), the first batteries were built at Hengdang and Nanshan on the Guangzhou coast.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，以廣東戰船年久失修，諭疆吏加意整頓。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianlong, because Guangdong's warships had fallen into disrepair through long years, frontier officials were instructed to give them conscientious attention and overhaul.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 5 (1740), the throne ordered frontier officials to overhaul Guangdong's war fleet, long neglected and in poor repair.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，巴延三以各海口時有寇船出沒，於石棋村總口設立專營，與虎門營汛聯絡。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, Bayan San, because pirate vessels appeared and vanished at various harbors, established a dedicated garrison at the main pass of Shiqi Village, linked with the Humen garrison outpost.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 46 (1781), Bayan San reported pirate craft haunting the province's harbors and set up a dedicated garrison at the Shiqi Village estuary, coordinating with the Humen outpost.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，吳俊以東莞米艇堅固靈捷，便於追捕海寇，造二千五百石大米艇四十七艘，二千石中米艇二十六艘，一千五百石小米艇二十艘，分佈上下洋面，配置水兵，常年巡緝。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, Wu Jun, because Dongguan rice boats were sturdy, nimble, and convenient for pursuing sea bandits, built forty-seven large rice boats of 2,500 shi, twenty-six medium rice boats of 2,000 shi, and twenty small rice boats of 1,500 shi, distributed across the upper and lower sea surfaces, manning them with naval troops for year-round patrol and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 58 (1793), Wu Jun commissioned a fleet of Dongguan rice boats—sturdy and fast, ideal for chasing pirates: forty-seven large vessels of 2,500 shi, twenty-six medium ones of 2,000 shi, and twenty small ones of 1,500 shi. Scattered across the coastal waters and manned with naval troops, they patrolled year-round.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，於沙角建砲台。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing, a battery was built at Shajiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 (1800), a battery was erected at Shajiao.

sentences.zh: 九年，倭什布以粵海窮漁伺刦商船，遇水師大隊出巡，輒登陸肆擾，遂無寧歲，乃規畫水陸緝捕事宜。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Aishibuo, because impoverished fishermen along the Guangdong coast waited to rob merchant vessels, and whenever a large naval force went out on patrol they would come ashore to rampage—so there was no year of peace—drew up plans for joint land-and-sea pursuit and capture.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 9 (1804), Aishibuo reported that destitute fishermen preyed on merchant ships and, whenever the main fleet put to sea, pillaged the coast instead—leaving the province without a peaceful year. He drew up a coordinated land-and-sea suppression plan.

sentences.zh: 十五年，設水師提督駐虎門，扼中路要區，以二營駐香山，一營駐大鵬，為左右翼。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, a naval grand coordinator was established stationed at Humen, holding the vital central zone; two battalions were garrisoned at Xiangshan and one at Dapeng as left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 15 (1810), a naval commander-in-chief was posted at Humen to hold the central choke point, with two battalions at Xiangshan and one at Dapeng as the left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 二十年，就橫當砲台加築月台，又於南山之西北，增建鎮遠砲台，置砲多具。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, a barbette was added to the Hengdang battery; northwest of Nanshan, Zhenyuan battery was newly built, with many guns emplaced.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 20 (1815), a barbette was added to the Hengdang battery, and Zhenyuan battery was built northwest of Nanshan, mounting a large complement of guns.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，建大虎山砲台，置砲三十二具。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Dahu Mountain battery was built, with thirty-two guns emplaced.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 22 (1817), Dahu Mountain battery was built with thirty-two guns.

sentences.zh: 道光十年，於大角山增建砲台一，置砲十六具。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Daoguang, one battery was added at Dajiao Mountain, with sixteen guns emplaced.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 10 (1830), a new battery was added on Dajiao Mountain with sixteen guns.

sentences.zh: 十五年，在虎門砲台置六千斤以上大砲四十具。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, at Humen battery, forty large cannon of more than six thousand jin were emplaced.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 15 (1835), Humen mounted forty heavy guns of over six thousand jin each.

sentences.zh: 又於南山威遠砲台前環築月台，亦置砲位於橫當之陰，及對岸蘆灣山，增建永安、鞏固二砲台，沙角、大角並增建瞭望台。

translations.literal: Also, before Weiyuan battery at Nanshan a barbette was built in a ring; gun positions were also set on the shaded side of Hengdang and on Luwan Mountain across the channel; Yong'an and Gonggu batteries were newly built; at Shajiao and Dajiao, lookout towers were also added.
translations.idiomatic: A barbette ring was built before Weiyuan battery at Nanshan; gun positions were added on the lee side of Hengdang and on Luwan Mountain across the channel; Yong'an and Gonggu batteries were erected; and watchtowers were added at Shajiao and Dajiao.

sentences.zh: 十九年，林則徐籌防粵海，以零丁洋入口之要隘數重，歷年雖增築砲台，而武山、橫當海面較狹，設大木排八千排，分為二道，大鐵練七百丈，臨以砲台，輔以水兵，以阻敵船來路。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Lin Zexu planned defense of the Guangdong sea, noting that though vital passes at Lintingyang's entrance were many layers deep and batteries had been added over the years, the sea surface at Wushan and Hengdang was relatively narrow; he set up eight thousand large log rafts in two lanes, with seven hundred zhang of great iron chains, backed by batteries and supported by naval troops, to block the enemy ships' approach route.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 19 (1839), Lin Zexu planned the province's coastal defense. Though the approach from Lintingyang had multiple fortified passes and batteries had been added over the years, the waters at Wushan and Hengdang were narrow enough to block: eight thousand great timber rafts in two rows, seven hundred zhang of heavy iron chain, batteries covering the line, and naval troops in support—to cut off the enemy's path.

sentences.zh: 時鄧廷楨因虎門當粵海中路，亦於橫當山前海狹之處，增設練排。

translations.literal: At that time Deng Tingzhen, because Humen stood at the middle route of Guangdong's sea, also added chain-linked rafts where the sea was narrow before Hengdang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzhen, noting that Humen guarded the middle of the Guangdong coast, also deployed chain-linked rafts where the channel narrowed before Hengdang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 又於武山下威遠、鎮遠二砲台之間，增大砲台一座，置砲六十具，以護排練。

translations.literal: Also, between Weiyuan and Zhenyuan batteries below Wushan, one large battery was added, with sixty guns emplaced, to protect the raft chains.
translations.idiomatic: Between Weiyuan and Zhenyuan batteries below Wushan, a large battery mounting sixty guns was added to protect the chain barrier.

sentences.zh: 二十年，林則徐以大鵬營所轄尖沙嘴一帶海門島嶼，為海舶東赴惠、潮，北往閩、浙所必經，乃於尖沙嘴之石腳上官涌偏南之處，皆建砲台，並藥庫兵房。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Lin Zexu, because the sea-gate islands around Jianshazui under Dapeng garrison's jurisdiction were routes sea vessels heading east to Hui and Chao or north to Fujian and Zhejiang must pass, built batteries at Shijiao and Shangyong south of Jianshazui, along with powder magazines and barracks.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 20 (1840), Lin Zexu recognized that the islands around Jianshazui under Dapeng garrison's jurisdiction lay on the route of every ship heading east to Huizhou and Chaozhou or north to Fujian and Zhejiang. He built batteries at Shijiao and Shangyong south of Jianshazui, with powder magazines and barracks.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，祁等以廣東民風宜於團練，招集已得十萬人，以昇平社學為團練總匯之所，推及韶州、廉州等處。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Qi and others, noting that Guangdong's popular customs suited militia training, had already recruited a hundred thousand men, taking Shengping Community School as the central gathering place for militia training, extending the practice to Shaozhou, Lianzhou, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 23 (1843), Qi and others argued that Guangdong's folk tradition suited local militia organization; they had already mustered a hundred thousand men, with Shengping Community School as the training headquarters, and extended the program to Shaozhou, Lianzhou, and beyond.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，增築高要縣屬琴沙砲台，並虎門廣濟墟兵卡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Qinsha battery under Gaoyao county was expanded, along with the Guangji market military checkpoint at Humen.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 27 (1847), Qinsha battery in Gaoyao county was strengthened, and a military checkpoint was added at Guangji market near Humen.

sentences.zh: 同治十年，瑞麟以欽州海面與越南接界，調撥兵輪，會同舟師巡洋。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi, Ruilin, because Qinzhou's sea surface bordered Vietnam, allocated gunboats to patrol jointly with the naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 10 (1871), Ruilin deployed gunboats to patrol the Qinzhou coast jointly with the navy, since those waters bordered Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 時閩、滬二廠兵輪次第告成，粵省亦仿造兵輪，以備巡防。

translations.literal: At that time the gunboats of the Fujian and Shanghai arsenals were successively completed; Guangdong province also copied their design to build gunboats for patrol and defense.
translations.idiomatic: By then the gunboats of the Fujian and Shanghai shipyards were coming off the ways one after another; Guangdong built its own on the same pattern for coastal patrol.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，劉坤一修整大黃窖及中流砥柱、虎門各砲台，威遠及下橫當共築砲台六十餘座，沙角及浮舟山各砲台亦依次建築。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu, Liu Kunyi renovated batteries at Dahuangjiao, Zhongliudizhu, and Humen; at Weiyuan and Xiahengdang more than sixty batteries were built in all; batteries at Shajiao and Fuzhou Mountain were also built in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 (1880), Liu Kunyi overhauled the batteries at Dahuangjiao, Zhongliudizhu, and Humen; more than sixty batteries were built at Weiyuan and Xiahengdang combined; and batteries at Shajiao and Fuzhou Mountain followed in turn.

sentences.zh: 八年，曾國荃以瓊、廉二郡洋面，與越南沿海相通，撥兵輪八艘，拖船二艘，赴北海駐防。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Zeng Guoquan, because the sea surfaces of Qiong and Lian prefectures connected with Vietnam's coast, allocated eight gunboats and two tugboats to garrison at Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8 (1882), Zeng Guoquan stationed eight gunboats and two tugs at Beihai, noting that the waters off Qiongzhou and Lianzhou connected with the Vietnamese coast.

sentences.zh: 九年，國荃以虎門為省城門戶，而黃埔、長洲、白兔、輪岡、魚珠、沙路尤為要區，乃於南岸屯重兵，為砲台犄角，兼顧後路。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Guoquan, because Humen was the gateway to the provincial capital, and Huangpu, Changzhou, Baitu, Lungang, Yuzhu, and Shalu were especially vital zones, stationed heavy troops on the south bank as flank batteries for mutual support, also covering the rear route.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 (1883), Zeng Guoquan posted heavy forces on the south bank, treating Humen as the capital's gateway and Huangpu, Changzhou, Baitu, Lungang, Yuzhu, and Shalu as especially critical points—batteries arranged in mutual support while guarding the rear approaches.

sentences.zh: 十年，彭玉麟辦理廣東軍務，就粵省原有各砲台，修整改造，並於砲台後辟山開路，以藏弁兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Peng Yulin managed Guangdong military affairs, renovating and converting the province's existing batteries, and also cutting roads through the hills behind the batteries to conceal officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 (1884), Peng Yulin took charge of Guangdong's military affairs, renovating the province's existing batteries and cutting roads through the hills behind them to shelter troops from enemy fire.

sentences.zh: 築綿亙牆濠，聯絡各砲台聲勢。

translations.literal: Continuous walls and moats were built, linking the mutual force of the various batteries.
translations.idiomatic: Continuous walls and moats were built to link the batteries into a single defensive line.

sentences.zh: 自虎門、大角、沙角以次各隘，節節設防。

translations.literal: From Humen, Dajiao, and Shajiao downward through each pass, defenses were set at every stage.
translations.idiomatic: From Humen, Dajiao, and Shajiao on down, every pass along the line was fortified in turn.
